items.quote: Market demand was robust in Q2 C26, though we expect a gradual slowing down of growth over the next few quarters as the effect of GST cuts tapers down and the negative impact of an expected below normal monsoon season starts impacting rural incomes.

items.statement: India growth impacted by aluminum portfolio restructuring (letting go loss-making products) and second consecutive quarter of export underperformance.
items.quote: One, the restructuring of our business portfolio at our aluminum vertical, wherein we have let go of some loss-making products. So that we are below market growth rate as far as two -wheelers is concerned. Exports ha s been a dampener for the second successive quarter

items.statement: Iron foundry export project ramp-up started; revenue recognition from next quarter; targeting INR2 billion annual turnover.
items.quote: We are now ramping up one big program for our American customers. So this will give us around INR2,000 million per year of new turnover that will fulfill our capacities in the country.

items.statement: Chinese OEMs gaining share in Europe (10-12% of registrations) threatens European supplier base; CIE engaging with Chinese OEMs for future localization.
items.quote: As of now, the Chinese OEMs don't have a supply chain in Europe. And as we see it for the next 2 years, the more market share Chinese gain, European automotive suppliers, auto component suppliers are at a disadvantage.

items.statement: Consolidated net financial debt negative INR14.2 billion (net cash) at end of H1 CY26; actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.
items.quote: The consolidated net financial debt at the end of H1 C26 was negative INR14.2 billion, which means we have healthy liquid cash available, and we are actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: Greenfield expansions under evaluation in two verticals driven by customer location requests; brownfield and pure expansions preferred for speed.
items.quote: The greenfields we are looking at in two different verticals, and that is because our customers are asking us to move to a new location. We have enough land in our existing plant. So wherever possible, we are looking at brownfields and pure expansions beca use as you know, that makes it faster

items.statement: Targets at least 30% presales growth for FY27, possibly better if launches happen on time.
items.quote: The last quarter, I mean, like end of the financial year, so we have guided for at least 30% growth in the presales. That I think we should be able to continue to achieve.

items.statement: Plans to complete 6-6.5 million sq ft in FY27 versus 5.4 million sq ft last year.
items.quote: We plan to complete about 6 to 6.5 million square feet for FY ’27 as against last year’s completion of about 5.4 million square feet, which can be about 20% higher.

items.statement: Confident of launching 9 projects totaling ~8.2 million sq ft in remaining FY27, GDV ~INR12,000 crores.
items.quote: Of this, we are confident of launching 9 projects, aggregating approximately 8.2 million square feet during the remaining period of FY ’27.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to improve to 17-20% by Q4 FY27 from current 9.7%.
items.quote: So, our expectation is that by Q4, as we currently, we are at about 9.7% EBITDA. So, as we leave the end of Q4, maybe hopefully, we should be able to do closer towards 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Land investment could reach INR1,500-1,600 crores this year if Bangalore and NCR deals close.
items.quote: So, if we are able to complete those transactions, then we might look at closer towards INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores this year.

items.statement: INR1,000 crores NCDs to be issued in tranches over next couple of quarters as acquisitions firm up.
items.quote: We envisage the usage coming in the next couple of quarters. So, we would do it in tranches as and when we identify the acquisition opportunity or, let’s say, firm up the acquisition opportunity, we would go ahead with the funding of NCD.

items.statement: Net debt expected to be around zero level for the year.
items.quote: We envisage our net debt to be at about 0 level for this year.

items.statement: Overall demand scenario stable; strong Q1 response due to better launch preparation.
items.quote: Otherwise, the overall demand scenario seems to be quite stable from what we have seen in terms of the launches and also what we are witnessing post the launches also.

items.statement: Margin cash flow lower for forthcoming projects due to higher joint development mix and absence of own-land Hoskote.
items.quote: So, the main difference for the new forthcoming majority -- I mean, the mix of the projects, a greater mix is towards joint development. And hence, that’s the marginal cash flow, you would have seen reduction.

items.statement: Forthcoming launch pipeline of ~20.77 million sq ft across 17 projects; unsold inventory 14.94 million sq ft.
items.quote: We currently have a forthcoming launch pipeline of about 20.77 million square feet across 17 projects.

items.statement: Revenue yet to be recognized from already-sold units stands at INR20,553 crores.
items.quote: As end of this quarter, the company has INR20,553 crores of revenue yet to be recognized from the sales that have already been done.

items.statement: Projected receivable plus unsold value ~INR31,000 crores; remaining cost INR19,000 crores; margin cash flow INR12,000 crores.
items.value: INR31,000 crores; INR19,000 crores; INR12,000 crores
items.quote: We have projected receivable from sale and unsold value approximately INR31,000 crores. Against this, the estimated remaining cost to be incurred is INR19,000 crores, resulting in projected margin cash flow of INR12,000 crores from completed and ongoing projects.

items.statement: Karnataka minimum wage hike may have small cost impact, expected to be absorbed within project budgets.
items.quote: However, it would have a little bit of impact on our overall cost. That is yet to be assessed. But I think we are considering -- it should be -- we should be able to absorb it within the budget that we have allocated for the projects.

items.statement: Other businesses revenue expected similar to last financial year this year.
items.quote: In the steady-state run rate, we expect, in this financial year also to be similar to last financial year in terms of revenue for the other businesses.

items.statement: Exports target to exceed 250,000 units per month from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: we are looking at moving exports to beyond the 2,50,000 per month level this quarter and onwards

items.statement: Capacity expansion of ~25% from 7 million to 9 million units per annum across businesses
items.quote: we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 20.9%, up 10 bps sequentially despite 4.5% commodity inflation
items.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment

items.statement: Pricing actions offset ~50% of 4.5% commodity inflation; balance absorbed via dollar realization and cost rationalization
items.quote: we responded with calibrated pricing very judiciously taken through April and June, enabling us to offset nearly about half of the inflation through pricing

items.statement: Domestic two-wheeler industry grew 14% YoY in Q1; EV scooters and 150cc+ motorcycles driving growth
items.quote: the two-wheeler industry turned in a resilient performance as registrations grew by 14% year-on-year in quarter 1

items.statement: EV portfolio (2W+3W) at 30% of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin; Chetak EBITDA positive
items.quote: Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double-digit EBITDA percentage

items.statement: Demand ahead of supply for Chetak; capacity expansion underway to 60,000 units/month immediately
items.quote: Demand, however, continued to remain ahead of our ability to supply. Capacity expansion has been undertaken, with an immediate and medium-term focus to enable us better serve the growing market

items.statement: Broader cost inflation spreading to proprietary components, electronics, labour, logistics and energy in Q2
items.quote: inflation is no longer confi ned to the base metals complex. The cost pressures have become more broader, with proprietary components, electronics, electrical parts, labour, logistics and energy and conversion now moving up simultaneously

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR21,000 crore at June end; INR10,000 crore paid out in July via dividend and buyback
items.quote: Cash on balance sheet was INR21,000 crores at the end of June. July is typically the month when we pay out the dividend. And last week, we've just concluded the buyback. Cumulatively, both those corporate actions put together would mean that INR10,000 crores in July would have been paid out to shareholders

items.statement: On track to deliver FY27 capacity addition target of 3 GW and capex of ₹20,000 crore.
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to deliver our FY27 annual target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex — having already achieved close to 36% of the FY27 capacity guidance, and surpassed about 87% of the total capacity added in all of FY26.

items.statement: Next year capacity addition expected in similar range of 3 GW.
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the same range. It will be in this range only.

items.statement: Completed ₹10,150 crore capital raise; ₹1,875 crore promoter preferential tranche pending until June 2027.
items.quote: This comprised three components. First, a preferential allotment to promoters of ₹3,000 crore, of which ₹1,125 crore has already been received, with the balance to come in before June 2027.

items.statement: Mahanadi expansion capex to be 25-30% lower than greenfield benchmark while doubling capacity to 3,600 MW.
items.quote: As compared to that, Mahanadi, when we will be completing, I can say definitely that we will be at least 25% to 30% lower while doubling the capacity from 1,800 MW to 3,600 MW.

items.statement: Received first large external order of about ₹440 crore for 5 GWh battery plant.
items.quote: On the 5 G Wh battery plant which we have commissioned in Q4FY26, we have received our first large external order of about ₹ 440 crore.

items.statement: BESS assembly margin expected at $2.75-3 per kWh, yielding ~₹150 crore annual EBITDA.
items.quote: So I think here, in terms of the margin in dollar terms, it's in the range of about $2.75 to $3. If you look at the overall capacity running, it will be about $15 million in a year. So that's how we are saying you can get about close to ₹ 150-odd crores of EBITDA from this project.

items.statement: India power demand grew 8.5% YoY in Q1 FY27; July month-till-date growth ~12%.
items.quote: India's power sector delivered a strong start to FY27, with Q1 demand growing 8.5% year-on-year — a sharp turnaround from the muted 0.9% growth in FY26.

items.statement: Long-term power demand CAGR expected at 5-6%.
items.quote: India's industrialisation, urbanisation, and rising per capita consumption underpin a clear 5–6% long-term CAGR in power demand.

items.statement: Hydro generation declined 26% YoY due to weak hydrology; recovery expected with monsoon.
items.quote: However, overall portfolio generation declined by almost 26% YoY, owing to weak hydrology across the entire basin — national hydro generation was down 7% YoY, Sutlej basin was down 39% YoY, and Ravi basin was down 24% YoY.

items.statement: Coal prices rose 25% YoY (API4 $113 vs $90); mitigated by shift to domestic coal.
items.quote: Coal prices witnessed a year-on-year increase. Taking a specific index like API4 as a reference, it stood at $90 in Q1 FY26 compared to $113 in Q1 FY27 — an increase of about 25%.

items.statement: Renewables now 61% of 14.6 GW installed capacity; thermal 5.7 GW provides baseload.
items.quote: With the sizeable capacity that we added, our total installed capacity now stands at about 14.6 GW, with renewables constituting around 61%, complemented by 5.7 G W of thermal capacity providing reliable, dispatchable baseload.

items.statement: Net leverage improved to 4.95x from 5.2x; committed to below 5x by 2030.
items.quote: Our balance sheet discipline continues to strengthen, with net operating leverage on a trailing-twelve-month basis improving to 4.95x, from approximately 5.2x in FY26, even as we scale up our growth investments. By year 2030, we are committed to have our net leverage below 5 times.

items.statement: Pumped storage projects offer significantly high-teen IRRs; capex ~₹5 crore per MW.
items.quote: In terms of when we say benchmark returns of mid-teen IRRs, here, I can say it will be significantly high-teen IRRs, we can say, is what we are absolutely confident with the tariff and the cost at which the most of the ordering has already happened.

items.statement: Housing.com to become profitable within four to six quarters; internal target three to four quarters.
items.quote: However, Aurum and Housing teams have developed an integration plan to make Housing LOOKUP in becoming profitable within four to six quarters.

items.statement: Company-level profitability possible in next two to three quarters, better guidance after Housing close.
items.quote: Yes, we do see the potential to be profitable at a company level because our existing businesses are already profitable, may it be in the distribution segment which always was profitable and now the rental segment is al so break-even at an adjusted EBITDA basis.

items.statement: INR 1,000 crores ARR target to be achieved faster and surpassed with Housing.com.
items.quote: Ishan, the INR 1,000 crores ARR target, you know, we feel that we're going to achieve that a lot faster with Housing.com transaction and surpass it a lot more.

items.statement: Revenue projections anticipated to be surpassed as flywheel adds consumers.
items.quote: But again, it's early days; we see a lot of ancillary revenue that is coming from Aurum PropTech into Housing and also Housing benefiting us at various subsidiary businesses, and as the flywheel keeps on getting us more consumers on the platform, we do, we do anticipate that our revenue projections will be surpassed.

items.statement: Tax rate and carry-forward losses guidance to be articulated in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: We will be able to articulate our clear positions in Q3, starting H2, when we are able to look at our long-term goals on the financial metrics of this business.

items.statement: PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins improved 1,320 bps, driven by fundamentals.
items.quote: PBT margins expanded by 1,590 basis points, while adjusted EBITDA margins improved by 1,320 basis points, reflecting the operating leverage beginning to emerge across the platform.

items.statement: Margins improved 1,000+ bps in Q1 FY27; unit economics to strengthen over coming years.
items.quote: Despite Q1 being the industry's softest quarter, our margins improved by 1,000+ basis points.

items.statement: Promoter subscribing to create INR 200+ crores war chest for Housing; not envisaged to be used.
items.quote: So yes, we'll have INR 200 odd crores of war chest for Housing, but I don't envisage to use this.

items.statement: REA Group now holds 24.9% after PropTiger and Housing share swaps; dilution to largest PropTech group.
items.quote: So, what we have effectively done, we have today on our cap table 24.9% shareholder which is probably the largest PropTech group in the world and one of the biggest media groups in the world.

items.statement: Housing.com annualized burn INR 200 crores; plan to streamline costs to break-even in 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: So as of right now, you know, the business as is, it's doing INR 200 crores of burn annualized basis. This of course, you know, once we close and we start our operations, the idea is to streamline the costs and bring it to a break-even point in four to six quarters.

items.statement: Housing FY25 revenue INR 343 crores, expenses INR 531 crores; FY26 numbers being audited.
items.quote: Having said that, if we look at the FY 2025 revenue from operations at Housing.com between the listing services and various other factors, INR 343 crores was the revenue as of FY '25.

items.statement: India has 2.5 crore property transactions yearly; 1.2 crore digitally addressable; only 7-10 lakh online intermediated.
items.quote: India witnesses approximately 2.5 crore s property transactions every year, of which nearly 1.2 crores transactions are expected to become digitally addressable. Today, however, only 7 to 10 lakh residential transactions are actively intermediated through online portals, highlighting how early digital penetration remai

items.statement: Housing.com has 24% online portal market share, 58 million monthly visits, 12 million app MAU.
items.quote: Housing.com already commands approximately 24% of India's online portal market, supported by one of the country's strongest consumer brands, attracting over 58 million average monthly visits and 12 million monthly active users on its app.

items.statement: Sell.do gross churn 7%, crossed 1,000 developers and 11,800+ active licenses.
items.quote: The churn at agross level was 7%, but Sell.do has been growing in terms of licenses as well as number of developers that are onboarded onto the platform. Sell.do has now crossed 1,000 developers onboarded onto the platform with 11,800+ active licenses that are there currently.

items.statement: Management maintains mid-to-high teens revenue growth guidance for FY27 despite strong Q1 performance
items.quote: I will still hold to the mid to high teens guidance at this point in time.

items.statement: Specialty diagnostics ambition to reach 15-20% of portfolio in 3-5 years
items.quote: our rough estimate is for most of our peer set, specialty forms between 15% to 20% of that portfolio. I think our ambition would be to reach the same levels in the three to five year timeline.

items.statement: Most specialty diagnostics capex already deployed in central labs; minimal incremental capex expected next year
items.quote: most of the investments are going into our Mumbai lab or our Delhi lab, which are our central processing labs. So that capex is already done. I mean, now it will be mostly expansion capex if the volumes increase far below -- beyond what we thought. But I don't anticipate the significant amount of capex going into this business at least next year.

items.statement: Franchisee network grew to 11,700 active franchisees with 900 net additions in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our franchisee base has reached its highest level ever at 11,700 active franchisees in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Franchisee additions expected at 500-700 per quarter for remaining FY27 with churn consideration
items.quote: you can consider 500 to 700 as an average addition every quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 32.2% in Q1 FY27, up from 23% in FY23
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter was 32.2%, with EBITDA growing 34% year -on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 290 bps to 74.1% driven by better negotiations, 28% test volume growth, and operational efficiency
items.quote: our gross margins at 74.1%, reflecting an improvement of more than 290 basis points over the year. This was largely driven from better negotiations, strong 28% growth in task volume, and improved operation efficiency.

items.statement: Pathology business grew 26% YoY in Q1 FY27 with franchisee and partnership segments both growing over 25%
items.quote: our pathology business has grown even faster at 26%.

items.statement: Non-Aarogyam portfolio growing faster than Aarogyam; shift toward semi-specialized tests improving realization
items.quote: Aarogyam has grown slower than non-Aarogyam. And that is actually linked to the question that I just -- which was Aarogyam as a realization because there are so many tests and all of that typically tends to be dilutive to the revenue per while that we get from franchisees.

items.statement: Nuclear Healthcare divestment process expected to take at least 6 months; no definitive buyer yet
items.quote: I anticipate the process will take 6 months, right? But we don't have any definitive what you call buyer at this point in time.

items.statement: ESOP charge stabilized at ~INR 3.5 crores per quarter
items.quote: ESOPs charge -- so it would be around 3.5 crores in the P&L quarter. And now why we have stopped reporting is because now what we feel is this has stabilized now.

items.statement: Cumulative capex investment of INR 250+ crores over last 5 years while expanding EBITDA margins
items.quote: Importantly, we have achieved all this while continuing to invest in our business INR250 crores plus of capex investments and required opex investment to execute all the initiatives which we want to and so to ensure, strengthen reach, reliability, and Poverty.

items.statement: Radiology business PAT expected at INR 6 crores for FY27
items.quote: I think INR6 crores PAT is what we can expect for the year, not more.

items.statement: API Holdings debt reduced from INR 1,700 crores to INR 1,050 crores; IPO consideration only when profitable ex-Thyrocare and debt-free
items.quote: were at INR1,700 crores debt last year. We are now INR1,800 crores debt last year. We are now down to INR1,050 crores. And as you -- if you have been following, we have been, what you call, selling nonstrategic assets, seeing what all options are there to monetize to bring down the right? I think API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex -Thyrocare, as well as debt free

items.statement: Thyrocare branded consumables strategy to be announced by September
items.quote: It will be in the direction of Thyrocare branded consumables, not backward integration. But this is a matter of internal strategy. So, I would request please be patient. By September, you will see an announcement from us

items.statement: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 10% to 15%, with similar growth expected in profits.
items.quote: So we can -- the growth rate is around 10% to 15% for the next this quarter, this year 2027.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to reach INR900-1,000 crores in the next two to three years.
items.quote: Down the next two to three years, you can expect anything around INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Management plans annual capex of INR40-50 crores every year going forward.
items.quote: So the capex will be every year we are allocating around INR40 crores to INR50 crores for next every year, it will be like INR40 crores to INR50 crores capital expenditure.

items.statement: Peptide plant at full utilization expected to generate INR200-300 crores revenue at 18-20% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Once we are to a peak and full utilization of plant, we can expect anything around INR200 crores to INR300 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Cenobamate launch expected to contribute INR10-12 crores revenue in FY27.
items.quote: So the launching quantity and put together this year, it will be around INR10 crores to INR12 crores.

items.statement: Peptide facility with 250 kg per annum capacity targeted for commissioning by Q4 2027, first producing Semaglutide.
items.quote: To commercialize this pipeline, we are getting up a dedicated peptide manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 250 kg per annum, targeted for commissioning by Q4 2027.

items.statement: Oncology API dedicated manufacturing facility targeted for commercialization by Q4 2028.
items.quote: Another key focus area is oncology API where we are building a dedicated manufacturing facility which will commercialize and the target date by Q4 2028.

items.statement: Export share expected to grow from current 18-20% to 30-35% of revenue in near future.
items.quote: So in near future, you can see exports growing to around 30% to 35% and rest will be domestic and formulation.

items.statement: Magnesium L-Threonate business expected to grow 15-20% in FY27.
items.quote: There's a growth of around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: API prices remained stable this quarter; future direction depends on geopolitical situation and oil prices.
items.quote: The API price has been more or less stable during this last quarter as compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Receivable days improved from 145 to 131 days; management anticipates further reduction to 110-120 days.
items.quote: We have come down from 145 days to 131 days as of quarter one of this year. We continue to work with our customers to improve this much further, but we anticipate it to be around 110 to 120 days going forward.

items.statement: Backward integration on 8-10 molecules covering 20-25% of revenue expected to improve margins by 1-2%.
items.quote: You can put together around 20% to 25% will come from that 8 to 10 products and there will be a marginal increase from 1% to 2%.

items.statement: Medium-term objective to scale AUM to INR500-550 crores by end of this fiscal year.
items.quote: Our medium-term objective is very clear, that is to scale AUM towards INR500 to INR550 crores by the end of this fiscal year while maintaining strong asset quality, capital adequacy and governance standards.

items.statement: Expects total revenue upwards of INR75 crores for full FY27.
items.quote: we should be able to deliver upwards of Northwards of INR75 crores on our total revenue in the end of the -- in the entire 12 months period

items.statement: Expects PAT of INR25-30 crores for full FY27.
items.quote: from a bottom line point of view, we should look at anything from a INR25 to INR30 crores kind of a PAT numbers that we can deliver.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds at 12.75%-12.95% by end of next quarter and 11.75%-12.5% by year end.
items.quote: We are hoping by end of the next financial quarter we should be a t around closer to 12.75% to 12.95% and that out by the end of the year we should be at 12.5% between 11.75% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Targets NIM of ~3-3.5% quarterly (10-12% annualized) on MSME portfolio.
items.quote: Our NIMs what it was projected or we want to be at on an MSME portfolio is about close to 3%, 3.5% on a quarterly basis, it is about 10%, 12% in a annualized basis if I have to give that number, okay?

items.statement: Targets gross NPA not exceeding 1.25% and credit cost below 1%.
items.quote: We want to work our GNPA not more than 1.25% and we want to keep our credit cost below 1%.

items.statement: Plans 80% MSME secured and 20% digital lending portfolio mix.
items.quote: Our major portfolio will contribute 80% toward MSME secured portfolio and 20% is in our digital lending platform.

items.statement: Digital lending market for salaried borrowers is over INR50,000-60,000 crores.
items.quote: the organized borrower salaried borrowing our m ethod states that it is more than -- currently it is more than INR50,000 to INR60,000 crores okay.

items.statement: Plans to expand digital lending pin code coverage from 11,000 to 18,000.
items.quote: Today we have just opened pin codes 11,000 pin codes only, right. In the coming year we will touch this to 18,000 pin codes.

items.statement: Applied for PPI license, expects to receive it in 3-5 months.
items.quote: we have applied for a PPI license in Regency Fincorp Limited, we have got the approval, we have already applied for it in next three to four months or five months time we should get the PPI license.

items.statement: Aims to keep leverage at 3.5x-4x, may raise equity via preferential shares.
items.quote: we are very, very comfortable at 3.5x to 4x kind of a debt race, okay? We will not go beyond 3.5x to 4x of our leverage first of all, okay?

items.statement: Digital lending opex plus acquisition cost is 4% of APR.
items.quote: 4% is my opex plus my digital expense cost towards acquisition of a customer.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA breakeven in Express business this financial year.
items.quote: we are working very hard towards an EBITDA break-even in this financial year, and we are very confident that target should be achieved by us.

items.statement: Aims to reduce white space by 95% by September 2026 from 1.6 million sq ft.
items.quote: we are firmly on our track to achieve our glide path on reducing our white space by 95% by September '26 to the point where we started in quarter 1 of last year.

items.statement: Expects 150-200 bps gross margin expansion in medium term.
items.quote: We have said that 150 to 200 bps is kind of the expansion that we are looking at in the gross margin from a medium-term perspective, and we will continue to maintain that view overall.

items.statement: Plans to continue PAT positivity and improve operating performance.
items.quote: we will work towards continuing our trajectory of PAT positivity and improvement in operating performance.

items.statement: Sees strong tailwind from Mahindra's auto and tractor business growth.
items.quote: when Mahindra's auto and tractor business does so well, obviously, that has a very big tailwind for us. So, we will benefit from that. And hopefully, that will continue through the year.

items.statement: Winning new customers in e-commerce, manufacturing, and telecom verticals.
items.quote: we are winning a lot of business from e-commerce customers. So, we don't share that business wise, but I can broadly tell you that we have done very good work on e-commerce.

items.statement: Passed on fuel cost increase to 80% of B2B Express customers.
items.quote: Broadly, we have got the fuel escalation passed on for 80% of our customer even in B2B.

items.statement: Faced manpower shortages, site ramp-up, and wage revisions causing margin compression.
items.quote: the business has faced some headwinds driven by manpower shortages, site ramp-up and minimum wage revisions resulting in some margin compression.

items.statement: Last Mile Delivery revenue declined 16% Y-o-Y due to strategic exit from low-margin business.
items.quote: In our Last Mile Delivery business, LMD, as we call it, revenue moderation, we had a degrowth of 16% Y-o-Y was a conscious strategic choice

items.statement: Mahindra & Mahindra contributes close to 60% of business.
items.quote: We have close to 60% business from Mahindra.

items.statement: Withdrawing from Mumbai Airport taxi service as it didn't meet internal thresholds.
items.quote: we are withdrawing from Mumbai Airport. if you would have noticed, if you were transiting through Mumbai Airport, we had a Alyte service available. As I speak to you, we are withdrawing from that airport.

items.statement: ROA guidance revised to 1.2%-1.4% by exit Q4 FY27 from earlier 1.6%-1.8% due to external factors
items.quote: Based on this visibility available, we believe an ROA in the range of 1.2% to 1.4% of the exit of Q4FY27 would be probable.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 1.6%-1.8% for FY27
items.quote: And therefore, our credit cost guidance of 1.6% to 1.8%, that continues to remain. So we are not changing that.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance for FY27 at 14% with EEB 5-10% and non-EEB 20%+
items.quote: On the credit growth, what we had guided was for the full year FY 27, we were looking at a 14% growth rate, within which EEB, we were looking at between a 5% to 10% growth and non-EEB would be 20% plus.

items.statement: NIM stable at 6.2% in Q1 FY27 but may face moderate pressure from rising cost of funds
items.quote: This quarter also, despite challenges, we could maintain the NIM at 6.20%. But as I have told you that going forward, there may be some increase in the cost of the funds & cost of the deposits. So that may moderately affect our NIM.

items.statement: NIM improvement trajectory to 6.5% by Q4 FY27 challenged by external factors
items.quote: We had a line of sight towards -- we wanted to go towards a 6.5% by the end of Q4FY27. But given the fact that the cost of funds in the industry has gone up due to these particular external factors, that's where our revised guidance is to see how exactly we can maintain.

items.statement: Cost of funds rising despite no repo rate hike; savings bank cost up 20-25 bps QoQ
items.quote: I can also see that the effect of the reduced cost of funds on account of the reduction in repo rate that has happened and the benefit of which we have got till Q1 may not be available Q2 onwards because already the savings bank costs, the cost of funds have increased by around 20 - 25 basis points.

items.statement: IT costs up 65% YoY due to supply chain constraints from Middle East war
items.quote: We all know that the availability of chips, etc all these are impacting the Indian economy for that matter. And as you have seen that my tech cost has gone, I would say, high by 65% YoY.

items.statement: IT investment to continue; IT cost at 9.5% of total opex including depreciation, targeting 10% near-term
items.quote: Right now, and including the depreciation, it is around 9.5%. Management: Total opex: Partha Pratim Sengupta: Total opex. The industry benchmark for the mature banks, they remain in the range of 10%. Given that we still have a lot of IT investment to make, we will try and remain within the range of 10

items.statement: Target portfolio mix: EEB 33-35%, non-EEB 65-67%; secured 60%, unsecured 40%
items.quote: The portfolio mix, the strategy remains the same. We'll go to one -third that is 33% to 35% of EEB book and 65% non-EEB book. In this quarter also, you have seen that in the non-EEB segment, we have grown by 27% YoY. Our EEB has marginally come down, but the moderation has been much, much lower compared to the previous quarters. So, the strategy remains the same - 40% unsecured and 60% secured.

items.statement: EEB growth cautious at 5-10% YoY for FY27 due to macro uncertainty; non-EEB growing 27% YoY
items.quote: The challenge that we see right now is EEB, which for first quarter has remained flat compared to the last year. And this is where we will try and see how exactly we can step up the growth as the external environment improves further and our growth, which continues to happen in a calibrated manner.

items.statement: External risks: Middle East war driving energy crisis, higher funding costs, tech cost inflation, unpredictable monsoon
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical developments, particularly in the Middle East, a less predictable monsoon pattern, elevated funding costs and rising technology-related costs are factors that warrant close monitoring. These developments have the potential to influence customer sentiment, operating costs and overall profitability across the sector.

items.statement: Gross advances INR 1.56 lakh crore, up 16% YoY, 1% QoQ; deposits INR 1.65 lakh crore, up 7% YoY
items.quote: Gross advances stood at INR 1.56 lakh crores, registering a healthy 16% YoY growth, while deposits reached INR 1.65 lakh crores.

items.statement: Opex-to-assets at 4.3% in Q1 FY27 vs guided 4.2%; expected to taper after FY28 as tech investments yield returns
items.quote: Our guidance was that our opex to asset ratio would be around 4.2%, but we've already seen that it's hovering around 4.3%. So I think those are the two key factors which are leading to this reduction. But as we said, there are absolutely no efforts that we are putting of efforts that we are putting in terms of making sure that we continue to work towards the part that we need to focus on.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved sequentially to 29.4%; retail deposits 74% of total deposits
items.quote: CASA ratio improved sequentially to 29.4%, taking the share of retail deposits, including the CASA and retail term deposits to 74% of the overall deposits, further enhancing the stability of our funding profile.

items.statement: Gross NPA 3.1%, Net NPA 0.9%, PCR 86% including technical write-offs
items.quote: Gross NPA at 3.1%, net NPA at 0.9% and provision coverage at 86%, including the technical write-offs.

items.statement: Collection efficiency ex-NPA at 98.9% bank-level; EEB June collection 98.5% vs 98.6% in March
items.quote: At an overall bank level, the collection efficiency, excluding NPAs, remained healthy at 98.9% in June 2026. Within the EEB portfolio, collection performance was impacted by the usual seasonality associated with the first quarter, including a concentration of holidays during the month of April. Despite these temporary factors, the collection efficiency for E EB for the month of June 2026 stood at

items.statement: On track to add 5 GW greenfield RE capacity this year, excluding BESS and pump storage.

This includes the UTI Nifty 500 ETF and index fund, UTI BSE Index Sector Leaders ETF, and there are other funds which are in the pipeline. On the active side, we are looking at launching, subject to regulatory approvals, a balanced hybrid fund and some sec toral d

items.statement: SDOF IV AUM ~Rs 887 cr (target Rs 1,500 cr + Rs 500 cr greenshoe); MOF II launched, MOF I AUM ~Rs 1,599 cr; Real Estate Opportunity Fund I commitment Rs 189 cr
items.quote: UTI SDOF IV, launched in Q2 of FY26 and planned as a Rs 1,500 crores fund with a Rs 500 crores Greenshoe option, has currently an AUM of approximately Rs 887 crores. UTI Multi Opportunities Fund I has an AUM of approximately Rs 1,599 crores and is currently in investing stage. UTI Multi Opportunities Fund II started marketing in quarter t wo of FY26 and is planned as a Rs 1,000 crores fund with a

items.statement: Pension fund headcount to more than double over next 18 months; international headcount stable after 2024 US expansion; AMC headcount not expected to rise
items.quote: Pension fund, again, just to reiterate, actually over there the numbers will go up dramatically over the next two years, but that's just a function of the growth that we are seeing, and we think we can fund that growth quite comfortably without any profita bility dent when you look at the pure pension fund company numbers. So over there, we will actually significantly expand the workforce over the

items.statement: International business flows negative for ~2 years due to negative India sentiment and scheme underperformance; viewed as cyclical
items.quote: What you are seeing in terms of the flows over the last, I would say, actually, almost 2 years, combination of both the lack of appetite for India, I should actually say negative sentiment towards India and the fact that our own scheme has struggled in terms of performance over the last two years. So that's the reason why the flows are negative. But I see that as essentially a cyclical issue.

items.statement: No buyback proposal under consideration; maintaining cash buffer for potential bolt-on M&A in alternatives, international or AMC; no active talks
items.quote: No, there's no proposal that we are considering at this point of time. It's not on the table.

items.statement: Dividend payout ~95% of profit; expected to continue
items.quote: I think we have been maintaining a very healthy pay-out ratio of the profit in excess of 95%. I think hopefully that will continue.

items.statement: Flexi cap redemption pressure but SIP inflows encouraging; large & mid-cap positive net inflows; mid-cap fund positive net sales YTD
items.quote: There have been some redemption pressure under our flexi cap category, but large and mid-cap, we have been receiving quite a positive inflow, and in fact, in flexi cap fund as well, the SIP inflows have been encouraging. But while the overall net sales numbers are negative in flexi cap fund, but there are gross sales in that particular fund and large & mid-cap fund has been doing very well as far

items.statement: Pension fund AUM up 13% YoY to Rs 4.31 lakh cr; market share 24.16% vs 24.67% YoY
items.quote: Our 100% owned subsidiary UTI Pension Fund Limited has recorded a year-on-year growth of approximately 13% in i ts AUM, reaching approximately Rs 4.31 lakh crores as on 30th June 2026, as compared to Rs 3.81 lakh crores as of 30th June 2025. It currently manages approximately 24.16% of the NPS industry's AUM as compared to 24.67% at the end of quarter one

items.statement: Alternatives AUM Rs 3,843 cr (up from Rs 2,679 cr YoY); GIFT City feeder funds USD 206 mn
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, UTI Alternatives has an AUM with a total commitment of all active funds, including the co-investment portfolio manager, of Rs 3,843 crores, which is an increase from approximately Rs 2,679 crores in June of 2025. We have an AUM of USD 206 million as of June 2026 across two pooled vehicles in GIFT City, India Opportunity Fund I and India Opportunity Fund II, which act as feede

items.statement: CMD guided 25% revenue growth for full year FY27 with stable margins
items.quote: To conclude, we have started the new financial year on a strong note and I remain confident of delivering 25% revenue growth for the full year with stable margins.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin similar to FY26 full year level
items.quote: For current financial year, for the full year, as we guided during the commentary also, we are expecting a similar kind of margin as we had for full year FY '26.

items.statement: FY27 planned capex includes INR50 cr for electrolyte additives pilot plant and INR40-45 cr maintenance capex; R&D center and land acquisition capex to be announced later
items.value: INR50 crores and around INR40 to INR45 crores
items.quote: For FY '27, capex is largely the spillover capex of electrolyte additives as well as the pilot plant capex, which is around INR50 crores and around INR40 to INR45 crores of maintenance capex, that is what the already planned capex for this year.

items.statement: Battery chemicals plant trial run completed, commercial supply started; rapid ramp-up expected over coming quarters
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that we have successfully completed the trial run of our battery chemicals plant and started commercial supply. Demand here is unprecedented, driven by tight global supply and we, therefore, expect a rapid ramp-up over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Indichem plant construction ahead of schedule, capex completion expected by end of Q2 FY27, revenue from next financial year
items.quote: So this plant, we are happy to share that this is getting constructed even before the schedules and expected to get -- capex is expected to get completed by end of this quarter. And maybe from next financial year onwards, we will have the revenue coming up from that plant.

items.statement: Semiconductor chemicals demand structurally strong due to AI-driven CPU and memory chip growth
items.quote: What we are seeing is that AI is starting to push CPU demand higher and that's pulling memory chip demand up right along with it. At a time when supply is already tight. To us, this isn't the passing phase. It is a structural phase.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals margin ~24%, Pharma Intermediates margin ~36% for the quarter
items.quote: So with regard to margin, our Spec Chem business is having around 24% margin and Pharma business is having around 36% margin.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex INR56 cr: INR15 cr at Indichem, INR41 cr at ACL (battery chemical project, pilot plant, maintenance)
items.quote: capex for Q1 FY '27 stood at INR56 crores, out of which INR15 crores were at the Indichem site, remaining INR41 crores in ACL site, which is primarily diverted towards the battery chemical project at the Jhaghadia site. And then pilot plant at our Sachin site and maintenance capex.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives Phase 2 (third product) capex completion by end of Q2 FY27, trial runs soon, signed contract in place
items.quote: So for the Phase 2 of this -- Phase 2, which is for the third product of our Electrolyte Additives segment, which is going on schedule. And as we mentioned earlier also by end of Q2 FY '27, we would be completing our capex. So that looks very well on track, and we are expecting the trial runs to commission very soon.

items.statement: Battery chemicals demand exceeds plant capacity; 4,000 MT total capacity (2,000 MT VC + 2,000 MT FEC), full utilization targeted in 3 years
items.quote: So you know that the plant, we have a capacity of 2,000 metric tons for VC and 2,000 metric tons for FEC. So it's a total 4,000 metric ton capacity and for which we are more than confident that we will be able to hit the full capacity utilization by end of 3 years.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Gulf persist but raw material availability secured and supply continuity maintained
items.quote: We began the financial year on a turbulent note, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Gulf. While these tensions persist, our team has done a commendable work in securing raw material availability and ensuring supply continuity.

items.statement: Four validated CDMO products expected to generate revenue from H2 FY27, each INR50-100 cr peak annual revenue
items.quote: For these products, we have already mentioned that these are already validated products. And with regulatory approval in place, we are expecting revenue to kick in from H2 FY '27 onwards. And on a revenue potential side, these all products are expected to generate revenue between INR50 crores to INR100 crores for each year at a peak.

items.statement: Indichem semiconductor chemicals margin to be benchmarked against BFC business, not Pharma; premature to give steady-state number
items.quote: For the margin profile of Indichem business, I think you should not look at the API -- Pharma Intermediate business margin, but you should benchmark it with our BFC product or the business margin. It is very preliminary to give any number on this.

items.statement: Employee cost guided at ~INR150 cr for FY27 including annual increments and one-time performance bonus
items.quote: We should typically look at around INR150 crores of employee cost for the current year.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to remain at current levels (~16%) for most of FY27, with gross margin spreads around INR 28,145/KL sustained for next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: We are hopeful of the margins remaining at this level or around this level. The current quarter looks good. And we are hopeful of it carrying forward at these levels for the whole year.

items.statement: Volume growth target for FY27 is 8-11% YoY, consistent with historical range.
items.quote: Historically, we've always been doing volume growth in the range of 8% to 10% to even 11%. So, we see ourselves getting that much of volume growth during this year also.

items.statement: Export revenue contribution expected to remain at current elevated levels (~51% of revenue) for coming quarters.
items.quote: We anticipate the export revenue and the export sales will be in the same level for the quarters to come.

items.statement: Price increases implemented across all segments (PHPO, PIO, lubricants) except automotive lubricants where hikes were delayed; higher realizations driven by supply chain disruptions and agile sourcing.
items.quote: The price increase has been across the segment, except a bit for the lubric -- automotive lubricant category, where it is more of a dealer distributor network. The price increase has been taken even in that category but obviously got with a little delayed manner.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Middle East, Strait of Hormuz) causing supply chain disruptions, elevated freight/insurance costs, and raw material availability issues; managed via agile sourcing and inventory management.
items.quote: The operating environment remained challenging, shaped by heightened geopolitical tension in the Middle East, concerns surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, volatility in the crude oil and the base oil pricing and intermittent disruptions across the global supply chains.

items.statement: Texol subsidiary (Sharjah) temporarily impacted by regional supply constraints but maintained business continuity; logistics normalizing, throughput improving.
items.quote: During this period -- during the period of quarter 1, operations were temporarily impacted by regional supply constraints and disruption in vessel movements arising from the geopolitical situation. However, leveraging our regional sourcing capabilities and operational agility, we ensured uninterrupted supply to custome

items.statement: South Africa entry strategy under development; clarity expected in 1-2 quarters. New customer qualifications ongoing under NDA; pipeline includes domestic and international prospects.
items.quote: The strategy for the South African arm is being worked out. There will be much more clarity being emerging in the next 1 or 2-odd quarters.

items.statement: Trade payables increased to INR 430 cr but 90% within 90 days; INR 600 cr not yet due. Increase driven by revenue growth, not payment delays.
items.quote: Out of that INR900-odd the trade payables, there is INR600 crores, which is not yet due. On a basic -- historical basis, even currently, 90% of it is within 90 days.

items.statement: Targeting ~10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28; value growth depends on gold prices
items.quote: Broadly, we are targeting around 10% volume growth going forward. Internally, our primary focus remains on volume growth, and we believe that achieving around 10% growth in volumes is a reasonable target.

items.statement: Two new showrooms finalized: Dahod, Gujarat (~3,200 sq ft, COCO) and Jabalpur, MP (~3,750 sq ft, FOCO); fit-out underway
items.quote: We have successfully finalized the locations for new showrooms in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, and Dahod, Gujarat. All key agreements, approvals, and necessary formalities have been completed. Fit-out and showroom development activities are underway at both locations, and the stores will be operational soon.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.01% (+80 bps YoY); PAT margin 7.55% (+82 bps YoY) driven by scale, operating leverage, cost discipline, favourable mix
items.quote: At operating level, EBITDA increased by 70% year-on-year to INR93.99 crores in Q1 '27 as compared to INR55 crores in Q1 '26. EBITDA margin expanded by 80 basis points year-on-year to 11.01% as compared to 10.21% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Gold inventory carried at ~INR1,20,000 vs market ~INR1,51,000-1,52,000 (~20% gap); new procurement at INR1,45,000-1,50,000; profitability driven by making charges, not gold price
items.quote: As of today, if we look at the prevailing gold price, it is trading at around INR1,51,000 - INR1,52,000 whereas the inventory value reflected in our books is approximately INR1,20,000. This creates a sizeable gap of nearly 20% between the carrying value of inventory and the current market price.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth ~1-2% YoY; revenue growth 58% driven by gold prices; demand recovering after price correction to INR1,45,000-1,50,000 range
items.quote: When we compare Q1 FY27 with Q1 FY26, we have delivered volume growth of approximately 1% to 2%. The balance growth has largely been driven by higher gold prices.

items.statement: Gold 80% of jewellery inventory (22K), 18K ~15%, 14K/other balance; studded (diamond) 6-7% of sales, target 12-15% by Mar'28; silver revenue +150% YoY to INR40 cr
items.quote: As of now our business is doing like between 6% to 7% of the studded mix. And we have targeted by March '28, we would like to increase up to 12% to 15% on an overall basis.

items.statement: Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026 creates near-term cost and demand sensitivity; long-term fundamentals intact
items.quote: While the recent government announcement and increase in gold import duty from 6% to 15% in May 2026 has introduced near-term cost and demand sensitivity, the long-term fundamentals of the sector remain intact.

items.statement: Inventory turnover 4.7-5.0x annually; 95-98% assets in inventory; operating cash flow negative due to working capital nature, expected to improve with scale
items.quote: Our business currently operates with an inventory turnover ratio of around 4.7x to 5.0x annually, which, in our view, is among the best in the industry.

items.statement: Hedging: real-time replenishment (3-4x daily), old gold exchange (natural hedge), Gold Metal Loans (100% for incremental inventory), MCX positions per research
items.quote: The company continues to leverage exchange led procurement of gold, gold metal loan, and hedging mechanisms on the commodity exchange platform to mitigate gold price volatility, support margin stability, and improve working capital efficiency.

items.statement: Targeting 20% volume growth for remainder of FY27 with EBITDA also growing at least 20%
items.quote: So, looking ahead, we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg back to INR 7-8 range from mid-May, supporting full-year margin recovery
items.quote: From almost May 15th, we are already back to INR 7-INR 8 per kg margin.

items.statement: Annual capex capped at INR 200-250 crore to support 20-25% volume growth
items.quote: We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year. So, this year also will be INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore in total.

items.statement: Q1 blended EBITDA margin hit INR 2/kg due to absorbing gas cost spike on committed orders; new orders at INR 7-8/kg
items.quote: We took a hit from INR 7 a kg blended and we came down to INR 2 a kg, wherein we absorbed all that cost.

items.statement: Cost-plus model with 30-40 day order book hedge; sudden gas cost spike absorbed on committed orders, new orders repriced immediately
items.quote: We operate at a cost-plus model wherein any increase and decrease that we take in our raw material or even consumable is passed on to the customer.

items.statement: B2C contributed ~10% of sales in Q1; target 25% of total sales from B2C (50% of low-carbon volume) with 20-30% higher EBITDA/kg vs B2B
items.quote: Customer response has been encouraging with these products contributing approximately 10% of our sales already during the last quarter.

items.statement: IHT/OHT combined capacity 9,000t (rising to 15,000t with OHT commissioning); targeting 50% IHT utilization next month, 60-80% by year-end; EBITDA INR 10-20/kg at optimum utilization
items.quote: IHT and OHT combined, right now we have 9,000 tonnes of capacity, which will reach to 15,000 tonnes with OHT commissioning.

items.statement: Gas costs remain elevated (1.5x average increase) but fully passed through in new orders; no inventory loss risk due to 70-80% order hedge
items.quote: Even today, our gas prices are escalated. We do not see any decrease in our gas prices today. All of that is still there. Our costs are still escalated but the only change is that all of that has been passed on.

items.statement: Operating capacity 680,000 tonnes; running at ~85-90% utilization sweet spot; 60,000t additional capacity available on demand; backward integrated equipment manufacturing enables 6-month capex lead time
items.quote: Our operating capacity as of today stands at around 680,000 tonnes, and we are pleased to say that we are back to the normal level of operations with steady and comfortable margins.

items.statement: Reiterated FY2027 guidance of low double-digit organic growth in constant currency and 24-25% adjusted EBITDA margin despite 120 bps minimum wage impact
items.value: low double-digit organic growth in constant currency; 24% to 25%
items.quote: we remain confident in our revenue outlook and reiterate our FY 2027 guidance of Page | 9 low double -digit organic growth in constant currency. On margins, we are maintaining our 24% to 25% guidance despite absorbing 120 basis points incremental impact from minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin at 24% after absorbing annual salary increases and minimum wage hikes; full 120 bps FY2027 impact expected
items.quote: adjusted EBITDA margin for Q1 FY 2027 was 24%, again reflecting Page | 7 the resilience of our operating model despite absorbing both annual compensation increases and initial impact of the minimum wage revisions

items.statement: Minimum wage revisions in Karnataka and Telangana estimated at 120 bps impact on FY2027 adjusted EBITDA; Q1 impact was INR 70 million
items.quote: Based on the current notification, we estimate an impact of approximately 120 basis points for FY 2027 on adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 free cash flow INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million
items.quote: We generated INR 3,161 million of operating cash flow during the quarter, and our free cash flow was INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million.

items.statement: Signed $35.3 million steady state ACV in Q1 across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo
items.quote: Turning to new wins, our commercial momentum remained healthy with $35.3 million of steady state ACV signed during the quarter across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo.

items.statement: Demand favors partners with healthcare domain expertise, technology, analytics, AI and ability to deliver measurable outcomes; traction in managed service deals
items.quote: Against this backdrop, demand continues to favour partners that combine deep healthcare domain expertise with operational scale, technology, analytics, AI and a demonstrated ability to deliver measurable outcomes.

items.statement: Minimum wage impact could change if notifications revised; deal timing for managed services unpredictable; pricing pressure from clients continues
items.quote: These estimates are based on the minimum wages notification currently in effect, and any revisions to the same could result in a change to the estimated impact.

items.statement: On track to fully repay outstanding debt during FY2027; net debt INR 1,110 million, net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA 0.06x
items.quote: We remain on track to fully repay our outstanding debt during FY 2027. This will further strengthen our balance sheet and reduce finance costs.

items.statement: CareSeed acquisition closed June 2026; adds HEDIS reporting platforms Forecast and Harvest, 26 mid/small payer clients, strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capabilities
items.quote: We closed this acquisition in June this year. This is a company founded in 2012, headquartered in Kansas City. CareSeed delivers on HEDIS reporting and has two platforms, Forecast which provides HEDIS reporting and quality analytics, and Harvest which delivers cloud -based medical record review and chart abstraction.

items.statement: No pricing levers exercised; pricing pressure from clients continues; revenue growth driven by volume and new services not price increases
items.quote: There were no pricing levers that we exercised, right? I've continued to say this in the past. Given the situation of our clients, the movement in prices is in the opposite direction, right? So there's more pricing pr essure than any price increases that we would get

items.statement: Broad-based growth across existing clients and FY2026 client additions; high-value areas like clinical driving growth; 5.1% sequential organic constant currency growth ex-seasonality
items.quote: After normalising for open enrolment revenues in Q4 FY 2026, our sequential organic growth in constant currency terms was 5.1%.

items.statement: AI implementation by payers showing only marginal improvements; 70% adopted AI but only 10% report measurable improvement; workflow redesign needed before agentic AI
items.quote: 70% of them claim to have adopted AI, but only 10% of them reported measurable improvement. What that really means is people who are doing AI implementation on a piecemeal basis aren't seeing the returns that they expected.

items.statement: Employee strength 47,307; voluntary attrition improved to 28.6% from 38.1% in Q4 FY2026; 65-70% headcount in Bangalore and Hyderabad affected by minimum wage revisions
items.quote: Our employee strength was 47,307 at the end of Q1, while quarterly voluntary attrition improved significantly to 28.6% from 38.1% in Q4 FY 2026, but was marginally higher than Q1 of FY 2026.

items.statement: ESOP pool of 3% equity over multi-year period; grants not yet made; impact to be reported in subsequent earnings calls
items.quote: The 3% is obviously not for one year. It's over a period of time for which the grants will be applicable. It will be in -line with what the rest of the market also sees.

items.statement: AI-led deflation historically 100-150 bps, could increase to 200 bps; driven by onshore-to-offshore migration, automation, and AI; not tracked quarterly
items.quote: even before we had 100 to 150 bps and that could increase to 200 bps over the near future and maybe even go higher in the future. But specifically, we don't have a means to track that on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Expect inflation impact to taper down in subsequent quarters of FY27
items.quote: With elevated inflation weighing on demand environment in quarter 1, we expect the impact to taper down in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: No further price increases planned at current inflation levels
items.quote: At this moment, we do not feel the need to take any further price increases beyond what we have already done.

items.statement: Plan to accelerate small format store openings, see opportunity for ~3,000 small stores
items.quote: We can see an opportunity of almost 3,000 small format stores in the country. And as we progress forward, you will see increased momentum on the small format.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4% YoY due to lower promotional spend
items.quote: On the gross margin, the improvement that you've seen this quarter from 28.4% to 28.7% is largely because of the fact that our promotional expenditure has been lower than the previous year.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved to 10.4% from 10.3% YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crores, which was a growth of 19.3% over last year, and our operating margin (Operating EBITDA margin) improved from 10.3% last year to 10.4% this year.

items.statement: Private brands to maintain or widen price discount vs market leaders in FMCG
items.quote: Our firm view is that our price discount to the market leaders has to be almost in every case, actually slightly higher than earlier or at the very least, the same.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 10% driven by 8% new customer acquisition and 3% existing customer volume growth
items.quote: Our total number of customer acquisitions in the quarter has gone up by 8%. So we have served 8% new customers in our store. And our existing customers have bought 3% more approximately in this quarter, and that's how we have achieved approximately 10% same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Private brands contribute 75.2% of revenue; 100% in apparel, 75% in GM, 60% in FMCG by volume
items.quote: Our private brands continue to see strong customer traction, contributing 75.2% to revenue growth or rather our revenue in quarter 1 FY27.

items.statement: RFID rollout across network to take slightly over 1 year; currently rolling out in Delhi NCR
items.quote: But I think the entire rollout will slightly exceed 1-year time frame.

items.statement: Employee cost per sq ft up 13% YoY due to minimum wage hikes across multiple states; structural change
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen a significant increase in minimum wages across multiple states like Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and so on and so forth. Obviously, the base has gone up, but we will continue to look for opportunities and try and optimize as much as possible. But obviously, this is a structural change.

items.statement: Closing inventory at INR 1,900 crores as of Q1 FY27 end
items.quote: So our closing inventory for quarter 1 is INR 1,900 crores.

items.statement: Targets ~30% SSSG over next four years and revenue of INR 12,000 crores in next four years
items.quote: We believe that is the most conducive environment for us to be able to deliver the targets that we have set off for ourselves, which is essentially almost 30% or so SS S G over the next four years and along with distribution growth taking the overall revenue to around INR 12,000 crores number in the next four years

items.statement: Guides 20% CAGR in store count over next four years
items.quote: So, I think we've guided to about 20% CAGR over the next four years in terms of distribution growth.

items.statement: Expects marketing spend as percentage of revenue to decline from 6.6% to 4.5-4.6% over next five years
items.quote: So, we believe that over the next five years, this 6.6% will go down to around 4.5%, 4.6% odd percent.

items.statement: Expects blended inventory turn to improve to 1.7-1.8x over next four years
items.quote: And as we are growing distribution or adding stores on a larger base, the dilution of new stores is going to be significantly lower. So, we've already communicated that our Q1FY27 | Earnings Call Transcript blended inventory turn should continue to improve and over the next four years should go to the 1.7 mix kind of

items.statement: Sees massive headroom to expand operating EBITDA margin from 7.5% to 15% handle over next four years
items.quote: So, there is massive headroom to expand the operating EBITDA margin from 7.5% to the 15% handle.

items.statement: Contribution margin has been largely stable
items.quote: I think what is important is to look broadly the gross margin and contribution margin, which is a more relevant metric, has been largely stable.

items.statement: Demand softened in May after customs duty hike but normalized through June and continued into July
items.quote: And we continue to see that the same trend continuing into July also. So, no major difference compared to what we observed in June.

items.statement: Stable gold prices are most conducive for consumer demand and business targets
items.quote: We believe that is the most conducive environment for us to be able to deliver the targets that we have set off for ourselves.

items.statement: Has not tried 9 karat; experimented with 14 karat in lower price points and redesigning entry price points
items.quote: we have not tried 9 k arat so far. And at some point - in - time we might, but right now we have not. We have seen, we have done some experimentation with 14 karatage

items.statement: Hedging policy unchanged at 50% of gold inventory; not designed to predict gold prices
items.quote: So, we are consistent with our policy, there is no change.

items.statement: 95% of products manufactured in-house; provides 300-400 bps margin delta but primarily strategic for design control
items.quote: Broadly all of it is in-house, about 95% of the products that we sell is manufactured in-house.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 39% in Q1 FY27, broad-based with older cohorts in line with portfolio
items.quote: One thing worth highlighting this quarter is our same - store sales growth of 39%, which was broad - based with older cohorts posting SS S Gs in line with the overall

items.statement: Repeat revenue contribution increased to ~60%, up 9 percentage points YoY; new customer additions declined to ~40k from 50k due to merchandise dislocation now improving
items.quote: So essentially, a lot of growth that we are seeing right now is being ably supported by very strong repeat in our business.

items.statement: Repeat AOV typically 20-30% higher than new; frequency stabilizes from second-third year; no material deviation across tiers
items.quote: I think repeat AOVs would generally be 20% to 30% higher than new.

items.statement: Long-term NMV growth guidance of 25% CAGR over next five years, higher in initial years and lower later
items.quote: So, I think we have a long -term growth guidance that we have kind of mentioned of the next five years of 25% CAGR, which is kind of obviously higher in the initial years and maybe lower in kind of the later years.

items.statement: Contribution margin to improve by restoring logistics pricing vs cost gap and growing ad revenue; efficiency gains passed to customers via lower pricing
items.quote: Initially or during the course of last year, some of our margin in relation to what we charge for our logistics services versus our cost had sort of come down, which we are now in the process of restoring. And beyond a certain kind of stage, we would largely kind of keep it constant and pass on any efficiencies that we gain in terms of logistics cost back to our sellers and hence customers.

items.statement: Logistics cost per delivered order fell ~INR 1 QoQ in Q1 FY27 despite fuel and minimum wage hikes; expect continued efficiency gains
items.quote: you would be able to see that our cost per delivered order actually came down even during this quar ter by about a rupee versus kind of the previous

items.statement: AOV baseline decline ~5% YoY; Q1 FY27 AOV declined ~2% YoY due to raw material and fuel cost pass-through
items.quote: During the course of a year as we kind of keep passing on efficiencies, the baseline AOV decline should be about 5% year-on-year. I think if I look at the last quarter, AOV declined by about 2% year-on-year.

items.statement: New initiatives (Horizon 2) annual EBITDA burn capped at ~INR 200 cr
items.quote: roughly about INR200 crores is kind of the annual budget cap that we have around new initiatives in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Valmo share of volumes ~50% in Q1 FY27, similar to prior quarters; no specific guidance on future share
items.quote: In terms of quantification, I think again last quarter was about 50%, similar to kind of the previous quarter before that.

items.statement: Annual frequency grew ~9% YoY with 29% ADU growth; both older and newer cohorts trending positively

items.statement: RAM share in advances increased from 58% to 59% YoY
items.quote: And you would have seen again in our Total Advances mix, our RAM percentage has gone by 1%; from 58% to 59% it has gone.

items.statement: FCNR(B) mobilization guidance $2.3-2.5 billion; $775 million raised in July; target $1 billion in July
items.quote: FCNR B you have said, we have given guidance of 2.3 to 2.5 billions of dollars. And against that guidance, we said this month, in the month of July, we will raise 750 million dollars. Against that already, we have raised 775 million of dollars. And within these 4 to 5 days left in this month, our endeavor will be to cross 1 billion dollars.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA expected to stay between 2x and 3x during the capex period
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA as on date, is slightly higher than 2 timex. We are expecting that net debt-to-EBITDA will not cross 3 times at any point. So this net debt to EBITDA level of between 2 to 3 will persist over this period of time.

items.statement: FY27 expansion capex expected near INR25,000 crores, FY28 near INR33,000 crores, thereafter more than INR35,000 crores annually
items.quote: This year, we are expecting that our expansion CapEx will be near about INR25,000 crores. Next year, it will be near about INR33,000 crores, and thereafter it will be more than INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: 56% of upcoming 24 GW capacity tied up under long-term PPAs, balance to be tied through ongoing and upcoming bids
items.quote: We have tied up 56% of our upcoming capacity already under long-term PPAs, and we are confident of tying up the balance capacity soon through ongoing and upcoming bids.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 continuing EBITDA grew 22% YoY to INR6,983 crores driven by higher volumes, improved PPA contribution and higher capacity charges
items.quote: Even with this, our continuing EBITDA grew by 22% to INR6,983 crores. Reported EBITDA surged by 36% to INR8,369 crores. This improvement was primarily driven by higher volumes and an improved PPA contribution.

items.statement: PPA tariff realization improved 8% to INR5.93/unit, merchant realization improved 13% to INR7.04/unit in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our tariff realization under PPA improved by 8% to INR5.93 per unit and merchant and short-term realization improved by 13% to INR7.04 per unit, directly benefiting from the strong demand environment.

items.statement: India Q1 FY27 energy consumption rose 8.4% YoY to 485 billion units, peak demand hit record 271 GW in May 2026
items.quote: Due to these high temperatures, peak demand shot up to a record high of around 271 GW in May '26, while overall energy consumption rose by 8.4% on a year-on-year to 485 billion units for quarter 1, FY27.

items.statement: Merchant volumes fell to 4 BUs from 6 BUs YoY as 1,200 MW (Butibori 600 MW, Tuticorin 600 MW) converted to PPAs; PPA volumes grew 30% to 25 BUs
items.quote: Merchant volumes were 4 billion units in quarter 1 as compared to 6 units billion in the same quarter last year, due to our tying up capacity in PPAs increasingly and incrementally during this period.

items.statement: Bangladesh receivables at ~USD400 million end-June 2026, receiving ~USD100 million monthly; receivables significantly reduced quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Specifically at the end of June, our receivable s level is near about USD400 million. We are expecting that every month we will also get near about USD100 million on an average from BPDB

items.statement: Total expansion capex program over INR2 lakh crores over next few years; FFO of INR20,000 crores annually covers majority, interim gap ~INR60,000 crores from debt market
items.value: INR2 lakh crores total, INR20,000 crores annual FFO, INR60,000 crores interim debt
items.quote: We are running a capex program of more than INR2 lakhs crores and on a yearly basis, we are generating an FFO of INR20,000 crores. So, in the same period as the capex program, there will be an FFO of more than INR1.4 lakh crore. There will be an interim requirement of around INR60,000-odd crores, which will be taken from the debt market.

items.statement: Target revised to 45 GW capacity (from 42 GW) on same timeline as earlier 42 GW target (by FY31)
items.quote: Yes. Now our target is 45 GW by the same time. It is now revised from 42 to 45. And we are confident that we'll be able to achieve it.

items.statement: Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW) expected before December 2026; Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) first unit Q1 FY28, second unit Q3 FY28 (targeting Q2)
items.quote: We expect that Korba Phase-II will come before December end this year. That is the broader expectation. As regards to next year we are expecting the first unit of Mahan Phase-II in the first quarter and then the second unit with a gap of 6 months going by normal standards, in the third quarter. However we are trying to bring that also in the second quarter.

items.statement: Acquired 180 MW Churk plant (non-operational), 24% stake in JPVL, 11.49% in Prayagraj Power; Churk revival ~6 months, meaningful contribution from next year
items.quote: It is not operational. It's like something like what we acquired in Butibori, more or less in the same condition. It will take some time, maybe 6 months or so. We don't foresee much contribution during the current year. So we have to revive this, and we can certainly expect a good contribution from it next year.

items.statement: Board approved QIP as enabling provision via EGM; no fixed timeline, will execute when market opportunity arises and need emerges
items.quote: The Board has approved this QIP, and we have requested our shareholders for approval through the EGM. This will be an enabling provision to be ready for this QIP. As of now, these are enabling provisions we have requested to our shareholders to approve.

items.statement: Nuclear power plans (10 GW by 2035) contingent on government rules under Atomic Energy Act; evaluating domestic and foreign technology; execution estimated at least 5 years once rules notified
items.quote: As I said earlier, only once we get the rules under the Act from the Government of India. We are keeping ourselves ready, but ordering can happen only when there is a clarity about the rules of the game.

items.statement: 13.2 GW long-term PPAs under bidding: UP 4,000 MW, Gujarat 4,000 MW, Uttarakhand 1,320 MW, West Bengal ~3,800 MW; more states expected to bid per resource adequacy studies
items.quote: The numbers you have already stated, the numbers stated on the slide, it already shows which bids are presently under progress, which is UP 4,000 MW, Gujarat is 4,000 MW, Uttarakhand is 1,320 MW, and West Bengal is almost 3,800 MW. So, 13,000 MW of bids are there now.

items.statement: Additional 3 GW capacity planned at planning stage to meet future state bids beyond current 24 GW tagged locations; JPVL stake increase possible
items.quote: So, this is just at a planning stage to take care of the forthcoming bids. As regards Jaiprakash Power Ventures, at present, since we have 24% stake, as and when, if we get any further opportunity of increasing the stake, then we will be in a position to take that forward.

items.statement: Fuel cost up 30% to INR9,513 crores in Q1 FY27 due to higher dispatch volumes and imported coal indices
items.quote: The Fuel cost for the quarter was higher by 30% at INR9,513 crores, which was driven by larger dispatch volumes and higher imported imported coal indices

items.statement: Revenue and EBITDA expected to be equal to or better than FY26, but conservative due to uncertain wind availability; Q1 was 7-9% lower YoY
items.quote: As far as this year's revenue and EBITDA is concerned, it should be better than last year. We are working on it. As I said in the answer to an earlier question, a lot depends on the monsoon and the winds. So, as of now, we look to be equal to or better than last year, but we have to see how things move.

items.statement: Margins sustainable around 60% as O&M, interest, and depreciation are predictable; Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin ~73.7%
items.quote: Yes, see the margins will be sustained because for us the O&M cost is more or less fixed. Interest and depreciation are also kind of predictable. So, margins are reasonably predictable.

items.statement: Blended interest rate at 9.1%; targeting 8.75-9% via refinancing and rating improvement; quarterly interest cost ~Rs 13-14 crore
items.quote: See, currently, the blended interest rate is at 9.1%. And the best rate which we got is for the old assets loan, which we took from HDFC, that was at around 8.2%. But current interest rates are actually slightly strengthening. Going forward, the interest rates we can make it around 8.75% lowest.

items.statement: Strong C&I and government demand for renewables; wind preferred over solar until battery storage economics improve
items.quote: We are still at a very low penetration of renewables compared to the target that is required. items.quote: See, I think as far as FY27 is concerned, we are adding 17.5 megawatts of solar and about 7.8 megawatts of wind. Plus, we have already added 3.3 megawatts of capacity in wind.
