items.statement: Wind availability in FY27 tracking similar to year before last (not as good as FY26); Q1 wind season muted due to delayed monsoon; Q2 matching last year so far
items.quote: It does not look at the moment to be as good as last year. It is probably as good as the year before last, but then we have to see. It's still early in the season. As I said, Q1 was significantly worse than last year, but Q2 as of now is more or less matching pace with last year.

items.statement: Evaluating multiple capital options: PE partnerships, strategic acquisitions, promoter rights/preferential issue; limited debt headroom (~20-25 MW more via leverage); Rs 800-850 cr carry-forward tax losses
items.quote: We have been in conversations with people on that. items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance range raised to INR 8,000-12,000 for FY28 from current INR 8,000-11,000
items.quote: But next year, we should be able to increase the range from 8,000 to 12,000. So, I can see profitability improving.

items.statement: Volume target of 255,000 tons for FY27 and 270,000 tons for FY28
items.quote: This year we are targeting about 255,000 tons for this year. Next year we expect to cross 270,000.

items.statement: Forging project with Aichi Steel on track, project cost expected to be >10% lower than estimated INR 475 crore
items.quote: From the INR475 crores that we had estimated, there is a substantial saving from that. The saving is more than 10%.

items.statement: Greenfield 5 lakh ton steel plant reconfiguration to increase capacity and add testing lines; cost per ton to remain similar despite metal inflation and rupee depreciation
items.quote: What was to be a 5-lakh ton plant is going to be significantly bigger than that. Of course, we'll have to make some more investments in that. But -- and cost per ton is going to be lower than what we had estimated in the new plant.

items.statement: Environmental clearance application filed for capacity increase from 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh tons; approval expected in 3-4 months
items.quote: We have applied to the Environment Ministry for approval to increase capacity to 360,000 tons of melting.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton at INR 10,700 (excl. treasury income); driven by cost reductions, higher volumes, lower job work
items.quote: If we remove that, our EBITDA per ton for this quarter comes to INR10,700.

items.statement: Price increases agreed with some OEMs for Q1, further increase requested for Q2; Q2 realizations expected higher than Q1
items.quote: Q2 will be higher prices.

items.quote: By end of this year, we will have the capability. So, we will start a second engine of growth.

items.statement: Greenfield plant timeline on track for FY30 commissioning but final cost estimates pending due to metal inflation, rupee depreciation, and added testing lines
items.quote: Metals have gone up everywhere as well as rupee has depreciated. So, the cost of specialty is going to be also based on that.

items.statement: Solar plant generated 2.3 crore units in Q1 (43% of power consumption); expansion of ~50% capacity planned in 1-1.5 years with lower savings due to new local content rules
items.quote: We expect in about a year or 1.5 years' time, we'll be going ahead and we'll be increasing the capacity by almost 50% of our solar plant.

items.statement: No customer concentration risk; Maruti currently ~10% of sales, target to increase share

items.quote: In terms of unit passenger revenue or PRASK for Q2FY27, with the current balanced demand-supply equation and the higher fares holding up, we are expecting growth of more than 25% compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 capacity growth guidance maintained at single digits as given at analyst meet
items.quote: Pulkit, we are holding to the guidance that we gave at the analyst meet. So, it's in single digits.

items.quote: No, we still hold to the mid-teens. That is going to be from FY2028 to FY 2030. It's going to be early double-digit to mid-teens levels is what we still are holding to.

items.statement: International ASK share target of 40% by 2030 maintained
items.quote: We have said 40% that we'll be there by 2030.

items.quote: We have signed a MoU with CFM International for over 1,000 LEAP-1A engines for future aircraft deliveries. This MoU also supports the development of our engine MRO and long-term material services.

items.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDAR came in at 38.3 billion rupees at a margin of 15.6% compared to an EBITDAR of 57.4 billion rupees and a margin of 28% for the same period last year.

items.statement: Growth driven by geographic expansion and new business wins plus debottlenecking of high-margin products
items.quote: So some of this particular growth has come because of incremental business what we could secure at different geographies where we were not earlier present. items.statement: Base business at new revenue plateau above INR300 crore/quarter vs INR240-248 crore previous quarters; Q1 seasonally lower but YoY growth 24% (18-19% adjusted)
items.quote: Q1 '26, we were around INR248 crores. Q2 '26, we were around INR240 crores, right? Q3, we were around INR245 crores. I think we've hit a new plateau, right? And that's Q4 '26 and Q1 '27, we've crossed that magical INR300 crores numbers.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing raw material availability issues and price volatility; intermittent line shutdowns; some customers resisting price increases
items.quote: What this crisis has done for us is raw material availability has become a challenge. So sometimes our lines are shut intermittently until we can get hold of the raw materials. Second is the raw material prices have gone up. Some customers have been kind enough to accept these price rises. Some customers have not been

items.statement: Reaffirmed medium-term AUM target of INR 50,000 Crore by calendar year 2028
items.quote: We remain fully committed to our medium -term guidance of INR 50,000 Crore AUM by calendar year 2028, confidence reinforced by the strength of the start we have made this quarter across borrower additions, asset quality and margins.

items.statement: Maintained FY27 credit cost guidance at 3-4% with cushion for West Asia crisis and monsoon
items.quote: When we gave a 3% to 4% credit cost guidance, obviously, we had 2 cut factors in front of us. One is the West Asia crisis. items.statement: Keeping FY27 guidance unchanged, will review after Q2
items.quote: However, we remain with the guidance today as it is so that we watch one more quarter before we take any further step on the guidance.

items.statement: May cut MFI pricing by 50 bps by end of Q2 FY27 if asset quality holds
items.quote: In our thought process, currently by end of Q2 FY27, probably can look at a 50 bps price cut if we are able to hold the asset quality.

items.statement: Further 50 bps cuts possible in Q3 and Q4 FY27 if credit cost trend sustains
items.quote: Maybe we may have to take 50 bps pricing cut in third quarter, maybe another 50 bps in fourth quarter. So it will happen gradually. It will not happen at one shot.

items.statement: NIM at 14.4% in Q1 FY27; may normalize to 13-13.5% if credit cost settles around 3%
items.quote: If our credit cost settles around 3%, then 14% NIMs may not be required. Maybe we may even do a 4.5%ish ROA with a 13%, 13.5% NIMs.

items.statement: Expect to add ~1 lakh borrowers per month going forward as primary MFI growth driver
items.quote: We added 2.5 Lakh new borrowers during the quarter, of which 35% were new-to-credit, and we expect this run rate to improve further, adding close to an average of 1 Lakh borrowers per month going forward.

items.statement: Opened 42 new branches in Q1 FY27, total 2,276 branches; employee base 21,981, attrition 20.6%
items.quote: On the operational front, we opened 42 new branches during the quarter, taking our total network to 2,276 branches, a growth of 7.7% YoY, spread across 457 districts. items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio 29.3%, PPOP grew 33.6% YoY to INR 873 Crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our cost -to-income ratio stood at 29.3% and PPOP grew 33.6% YoY to INR 873 Crore.

items.statement: Stage 1 PCR at 1.63%, expected to remain range-bound unless West Asia crisis worsens
items.quote: So I think Stage 1 will be 1.63%. It is the same this quarter. Probably if nothing materially happens, next quarter also, it could remain here until we get clarity on certain variables that are currently available.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining mid-double-digit revenue growth for balance of FY27 with 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.value: mid-double-digit revenue growth; 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: We are confident of sustaining mid-double-digit revenue growth in the balance of the year, with 30 to 40 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 44 bps YoY to 12.5% on 19.6% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Revenue growth is at 15.5%, and our EBITDA margin has expanded by 44 basis points.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~90 bps YoY to 56.7% driven by higher full-price sell-through and lower discounting
items.quote: Full price sell-through is up and discounting is down, resulting in a gross margin improvement of approximately 90 basis points to 56.7%.

items.statement: Consumer demand remains stable despite West Asia conflict; portfolio well-positioned in fast-growing casual lifestyle segment
items.quote: The demand environment remains stable despite the West Asia conflict. The investments we have made over the past few years in strengthening our brand platforms have improved the resilience of our business even in uncertain environments like now.

items.statement: Direct-to-consumer channels now 62% of sales (+380 bps YoY); online B2C grew 38% to 18% revenue share
items.quote: Direct channels now account for 62% of our sales, up 380 basis points year-on-year. Retail grew by 18% and online B2C grew by 38% in Q1.

items.statement: West Asia conflict poses supply chain, raw material, fuel and forex risks; monitoring closely with cost controls and potential price revisions if needed
items.quote: The continuing West Asia conflict remains a watch item for us. It has a potential to impact supply lines, raw material, fuel prices, and forex rates. We're taking active steps to mitigate and protect our performance, including very tight control on costs and a possible revision of product prices, if necessary.

items.statement: No immediate pricing action taken; long inventory cycle provides buffer but fresh buys for SS27 in next 45-60 days may require price correction if costs persist
items.quote: As of now, as we explained in our deck also, long inventory cycle protected us from taking any immediate steps. But obviously, we are very watchful. Any fresh buys, if things don't normalize soon enough, our commitments for SS27 are likely to be done over the next 45, 60 days. And if the prices continue as what they ar

items.quote: We are looking at an overall, from an annual point of view, we're looking at 1.5 lakh net square feet addition this year. From a sheer management of the portfolio point of view, the way we look at store additions, at the same time, we look at about a 5%-odd closing based on which are the catchments things are not worki

items.statement: U.S. Polo inventory bet paying off with strong performance; PVH global sourcing changes to mitigate geopolitical risk; inventory freshness at all-time high
items.quote: I would like to highlight that our bet on providing additional inventory in U.S. Polo is paying off, and this brand is consistently delivering a very strong performance. In addition to this, there was a change in PVH global sourcing in order to mitigate geopolitical risks. Having said that, our inventory freshness is a

items.statement: Inventory turns at 3.5x currently; targeting 3.7-3.8x in 18-24 months as channel mix stabilizes
items.quote: Yes Avinash, our current inventory turn is around 3.5 and yes, we are working on various things. We believe that with the current channel mix and whatever our aspirations are, we are hoping that in about 18 to 24 months, this should go back to about 3.7, 3.8.

items.statement: Other income normalized to INR 7-8 crore per quarter after Q1 FY26 one-time Ind AS 116 gain from COCO store closures
items.quote: Going ahead, we believe that whatever closure will be a balanced mix of stores, and we don't seem to be seeing any adverse spikes in other income. So, it is largely going to be stable around INR7 crores, INR8 crores, what we reported this time.

items.statement: Minority interest now purely from PVH JV after Flying Machine stake buyback; expect improvement as PVH performance scales through festive season
items.quote: You see, I think if you're looking at minority interest as compared to last year, quarter 1 -- there used to be a Flying Machine minority interest also, which is not there this time. So, what you see now is purely PVH Brands share of the minority interest.

items.statement: AI and analytics investments yielding early results in discount optimization and pricing; charter mapped for full year across consumer analytics and back-end efficiencies
items.quote: Our investments in analytics technology and AI are starting to bear very early results. We have mapped out the charter for the balance of the year. These investments will help us deliver deeper consumer analytics and bring meaningful efficiencies into back-end processes.

items.statement: Flying Machine relaunch on track: dotcom and app launch in H2 FY27; brand repositioned as denim-oriented Gen Z unisex with double-digit growth

We continue to build our brand proposition around Gen Z consumers, ensuring that we are providing for both men and women, more tailored to an on-trend expression with denim at its core.

items.statement: Internal ROA target of 1.5% for FY2027 but will not go below 1.3%
items.quote: Our internal target for ROA of 1.5%; but I am saying that we will not go below 1.3% for this year.

items.statement: ROE trajectory to improve from 12.7% in Q1, aiming to touch 15% Lakshman Rekha by year-end
items.quote: This year, we will try to touch the Lakshman Rekha, if we can execute it right.

items.statement: Repledger/LAS portfolio runoff from Rs.2,100 Cr to Rs.60 Cr; will be zero by next quarter
items.quote: That portfolio, which used to be Rs 2,100 Crores plus has now become Rs.60 Crores. Effectively it will get zeroised.

items.statement: Management declined to update FY27 guidance early in the year; will reassess in future quarters.
items.quote: I guess we're 1 quarter into our fiscal year. So, we will hold that for now, and we will look at how we progress through the quarter.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.5% in Q1 FY27, below guided trajectory; management expects recovery to 21.5%-23% gross margin range as transient items reverse.

items.statement: Volume growth expected to accelerate 10-15% in next couple of quarters as seasonality sets in.
items.quote: We were expecting the volumes to grow by 10% to 15% in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: New product portfolio (RCS, WhatsApp, IP messaging) grew 14% YoY and 11% QoQ, outpacing overall revenue growth of ~10% YoY.
items.quote: New product revenue grew 14% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter, growing meaningfully faster than the company as a whole.

items.statement: Heltar acquisition funded fully from internal accruals (INR 1,300+ cr cash); not material to balance sheet; expected to close in coming weeks.

items.statement: No further impairment expected; past bad debt issues resolved and not anticipated to recur.

items.quote: We were supposed to be done with the deployment and should have gone live by now. But due to certain reasons which are beyond our control, there have been delay in the deployment, but we're fairly hopeful that this quarter, we should be up and running with them.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 maintained at 0.8-1.0%

items.quote: At this particular point in time, we don't foresee an immediate change in pricing across products

items.quote: PAR has been slightly elevated in the last quarter more because of the fuel prices increase and also in terms of load availability due to the crisis in Middle East

items.quote: We are out in the market, evaluating our proposals for raising fresh Tier 2. We hope all things going well. We hope to close something this quarter

items.quote: As the platform gets bigger, we will pass on more benefits to customers. It allows us to tap into a larger market and that is where the additional MTUs will come from as well

items.statement: NAOV expected to remain flat; growth driven by frequency not basket size; low-NAOV assortment expansion offsets inflationary pull

items.statement: Blinkit growth primarily from existing cities; non-metros growing faster off smaller base but face less competitive intensity
items.quote: Most of it is from existing cities

items.statement: Discount-led growth creates systemic trap; customers acquired via subsidies leave when discounts withdrawn; no recovery path seen
items.quote: We don't see a recovery for platforms from this trap if they are acquiring customers by giving a lot of subsidies. There is no path to recovery

items.statement: Inventory losses at ~1.8% of NOV, asymptotic and not expected to improve materially; netted in gross profit

items.quote: Broadly, we are adding about 10-odd kitchens in a quarter, that's the pace of expansion there

items.quote: Much flatter than that

items.statement: District (going-out) in 5 categories; dining-out and movies largest; retail and events promising but early; smaller city footprint than food delivery
items.quote: Today, dining-out and movies are the bigger categories. Amongst the newer ones, retail stores and events could be the more promising ones

items.statement: Q1 FY27 results in line with full-year targets; strong OEM schedules indicate volume growth from September through March
items.quote: In general, if you see, our Q1 results are in line of our targets for this coming financial year.

items.statement: High-pressure mold line for foundry to start in Q3 FY27, doubling foundry capacity; axle shaft forging facility on track for September 2026 commissioning
items.quote: A high-pressure mold line for our foundry is expected to start in Q3. This will double our foundry capacity. Axle shaft production facility using material gathering and press forging technology is on track for commissioning by September 2026.

items.statement: Trailer axle prices increased 3-5% from April 1; further 1-2% hike planned for conversion cost increases; steel pass-through of INR4,700/tonne retrospective from mid-July
items.quote: It is approximately between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: OEMs indicating strong volumes from September through March across tractor-trailer and tipper segments; fabricators giving repeated and new orders driving 30% YoY axle/suspension volume growth

items.quote: If we look into our segment-wise revenue contribution, our trailers, axles, suspensions, and our tipping segment has contributed to 41%, while the component business stands at 59%.

items.quote: See I think in the markets from March exit to July, it has been flat. From June to July also it has been flat. So of course, there were certain price increases that have happened in between, but more or less everything got moderated.

items.quote: We do have inventory all the way up to middle of October. So, we know we can go all the way up to middle of October. What we have pencilled in is an ₹100 price hike. On account of fuel, it is ₹50, and all the other things.

items.quote: Overall, on a consolidated volume, we expect a ₹25 per ton, saving on that account, though at Jeerabad volume it could be ₹100, ₹125. The only asset which doesn't have a waste heat recovery is Andhra. So next couple of years, the target is to go for a waste heat recovery at Andhra.

items.quote: I think by end of this year, we should reach close to 60% capacity utilisation. So, from that perspective, we believe that Andhra might operate anywhere between 60% to 70% for the coming years, despite very high competitive intensity in the neighbourhood.

items.quote: The net debt as at 30th June has further come down to INR963 crores. This is sub-1,000 levels. So a reduction of close to INR100 crores from the last quarter.
