items.quote: So as of now, we see the retail spending to be fairly strong. It continues to remain strong, festival is still far away. Because of rains and monsoons, the final net result is yet to be seen.

items.statement: Corporate spend target maintained at around 20% of total spend, with focus on growing retail spend
items.quote: We have given a range. It will be 20% plus minus, and this is where we will be.

items.statement: No specific cohort stress seen, including IT sector; portfolio showing resilience
items.quote: Overall, the portfolio is showing resilience. There's no cohort per se, which is giving us concern as of now.

items.statement: Large tech investment in hyper-personalization made last year to drive retail spend growth
items.quote: And finally, last one thing which we have done is a large tech investment in the company last year, which we spoke about earlier, on hyper-personalization.

items.statement: Cards in force grew to 2.26 crores (7% YoY); added 1 million+ new accounts in Q1 FY27 (17% YoY)
items.quote: Cards in force have grown to around INR2.26 crores, witnessing a 7% growth Y-o-Y. In alignment with our stated strategy and road map, we successfully added more than 1 million new accounts in Q1 FY27, with 17% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: INR 70 crores overlay retained in Stage 1 provisions for geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: However, we are still carrying forward INR70 crores of overlay, keeping in view the current geopolitical uncertainties.

items.statement: FY28 growth aspiration remains at 15%
items.quote: Vinesh, that's an aspiration that continues. So there is no change to that. So we have 12.5%. The idea is that this helps, set up a good platform for the growth in 15%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 21.7%; operating margin at 17.5% impacted by forex loss and receivables provision
items.quote: We also maintained a healthy EBITDA margin of 21.7% while continuing to invest meaningfully in AI capabilities, enterprise platforms, talent, and go-to-market initiatives that will support our long-term growth.

items.statement: Adjusted operating margin excluding one-offs at ~19.75%, above guided 17.5-18.5% range
items.quote: Only for a pure comparison purposes, if I adjust these two instances, our operating margin stands at about 19.75% and higher than our not guided range but what I was saying as an expectation for us to be 17.5% to 18.5%.

items.statement: Demand environment mixed; discretionary spending selective but shifting to AI-led transformation, cloud, cybersecurity, data engineering
items.quote: The demand environment remains mixed with discretionary spending continuing to be selective. At the same time, enterprise technology investments are increasingly shifting towards AI-led transformation, data modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, and productivity initiatives.

items.statement: Key risk to guidance: prolonged geopolitical conflict impacting inflation and sentiment; AI capex reality check may trickle down
items.quote: I think it's the elephant in the room, right, if you look at the current war and the impact having on inflation and other things. I think that dragging out for too long is what I would see as a risk right now to sustaining the kind of performance that we've delivered in Q1.

items.statement: Target to increase capacity utilization by 10-20 percentage points by end of FY27, aiming to exit at 70-75% from current ~60%
items.quote: We are at close to around 60% as of now, and we would like to exit the year at around 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Plan to grow sales volumes by 5-7% per quarter, targeting 15-20% cumulative volume growth by end of FY27
items.quote: So, every quarter we intend to grow by 5% to 7%. So, at the end of the last quarter, we would have grown by 15% to 20%.

items.statement: New 40,000 MT oleochemical plant to start trial runs in Q2 FY27; margins expected to be better than current levels
items.quote: We are going to start the trial run. So, once that is stabilized, then we will ramp up the capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.14% in Q1 FY27; management expects current margin levels to sustain and sees operating leverage benefits from higher utilization
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 18 crores with EBITDA margin of 10.14%.

items.statement: Realizations increased ~25% from Q4 FY26 and ~30% from Q1 FY26 due to reduced Chinese dumping, supply chain constraints, and rupee depreciation; cost pass-through successful
items.quote: Realization from Q4 has gone up by around 25% and from Q1 it has gone up by 30%.

items.statement: Seeing strong export enquiries from 7-8 large global customers seeking supply chain diversification; export revenue currently 7-8% of total
items.quote: Around 7 to 8 big customers.

items.statement: Isostearic acid (4% of revenue) ramping slowly due to stringent cosmetic industry qualifications; expect commercial breakthroughs by end of FY27 at a couple of customers
items.quote: At a couple of companies, we have finished all five steps. At a couple of companies, we are at the fourth step.

items.statement: New oleochemical product (non-EV battery) to launch next quarter from in-house R&D; will improve dimer acid plant utilization
items.quote: Next quarter, we will be introducing one new raw material. Again, for the first time, we will be manufacturing that particular product.

items.statement: Management refuses long-term volume contracts without price commitment; geopolitical situation (Middle East) significantly impacts competitive dynamics
items.quote: I would not like to enter into any long-term contract with so much volatility. It would be hara-kiri for me.

items.statement: R&D spend ~Rs 50 lakh revenue expense (1-1.5% of sales); capex on need basis; focus on difficult-to-manufacture niche oleochemicals
items.quote: It's around 50 lakhs is only spent on the revenue side. The salary and the capital expenditure is on need-based basis.

items.statement: PAT guidance for FY27 is approximately INR 41 billion, representing 20% growth over FY26 PAT of INR 34.3 billion.
items.quote: In terms of our guidance for fiscal '27, that is 20% growth on last year's PAT of INR 34.3 billion and hence, approximately INR 41 billion of PAT.

items.statement: Medium-term PAT guidance targets beyond INR 85 billion by FY31, implying ~20% CAGR.
items.quote: Our guidance of about 20% PAT growth over the medium term, taking us beyond INR 85 billion over the next 5 years, i.e., by fiscal '31.

items.statement: Pre-sales guidance for FY27 reaffirmed at INR 240 billion, with H1 expected at 40-42% of full year.
items.quote: In terms of the rest of the year, we reaffirm our INR 240 billion pre-sales guidance for fiscal '27, and we expect H1 to be 40% to 42% of the full year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 pre-sales expected to be INR 50 billion or more.
items.quote: In terms of the immediate outlook for Q2, we are off to a good start in July, and we expect pre-sales to be INR 50 billion or more on the back of the planned calendar for this quarter.

items.statement: Data center infrastructure capex estimated at INR 500-700 crores over a period for the 3 GW park.
items.quote: let's say, a number of more like INR 500 crores to INR 700-odd crores that we will incur over a period.

items.statement: Launch pipeline for FY27 includes 20+ projects/phases totalling ~INR 250 billion GDV, including first NCR launch.
items.quote: For the full y ear, the launch calendar carries about 20 -plus projects and phases totalling approximately INR 250 billion of GDV, including our first launch in NCR as well as continued growth in Bangalore and Pune

items.statement: Embedded margins excluding land sales for Q1 FY27 are around early 30s percent; full-year guidance remains early 30s.
items.quote: The embedded margins excluding the land sales for this quarter are at around the early 30s mark.

items.statement: Expect residential pricing growth of 5-7% across micro-markets in FY27, with potential for additional 100-200 bps from brand strength.
items.quote: In the near term, we expect to enhance our pricing by 5% to 7% across different micro markets over the year.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East conflict could raise construction costs 1-1.5% annually, impacting project EBITDA by 35-75 bps if no price response.
items.quote: If this situation persists for a full year, we would expect project construction cost to rise by between 1% to 1.5%, with spread across a 3 to 4 year build period and assuming no price response; project level EBITDA impact of between 35 to 75 basis points.

items.statement: Middle East NRI demand (4-5% of sales) remains subdued; offsetting demand from NRIs securing India home base and US immigration-related buyers expected.
items.quote: The demand impact is quite moderate. Middle East NRI buyers represent about 4% to 5% of our sales, roughly a third of our total NRI business, and sentiment there remains subdued.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 pre-sales of INR 46.3 billion driven entirely by sustenance sales (existing projects) as launches were deliberately deferred.
items.quote: Pre-sales for the quarter were INR 46.3 billion, up 4% year-on-year. That is below our trend line, and I want to explain it properly rather than quickly. This was a decision, not an outcome.

items.statement: Premium and luxury segments contributed ~60% of Q1 sales; mid-income (<INR 3 Cr) now ~50% of portfolio.
items.quote: This quarter was no different with the lion's share of our sales of almost 60% coming from premium and luxury segments.

items.statement: Middle East conflict duration extended beyond Q1 assumption; impact contained but uncertainty persists.
items.quote: In terms of where the Middle East situation stands now, the conflict has not resolved by the end of Q1 as we had assumed. Let me give you an updated assessment rather than just assume that everything is normalized.

items.statement: Data center land monetization: 130 acres sold; further 150 acres to be monetized over 3-4 years at ~INR 600M/acre (~INR 90B sales) to fund 1 GW powered shell.
items.quote: Of this, about 130 acres has now been sold, and we expect to monetize a further 150 acres over the next 3 to 4 years at an average of about INR 600 million per a cre, generating approximately INR 90 billion of further sales just from Phase 1 of our land

items.statement: RentCo exit run rate target >INR 30B by FY32 (10x from INR 3B), driven by INR 20B+ from data centers, INR 6B retail/office, INR 4B warehousing.
items.quote: The target is over INR30 billion, i.e., 10x by fiscal '32, of which about INR20 billion plus will come from data centers, INR6 billion from retail and offices and about INR4 billion from warehousing and industrial.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 4.5B to under INR 50B; net debt/equity at 0.2x vs 0.5x ceiling; DevCo targets net debt free in 2-3 years.
items.quote: After investments, we still reduced net debt by INR 4.5 billion to now under INR 50 billion. Net debt to equity now stands at approximately 0.2x against our self-imposed ceiling of 0.5x.

items.statement: Net order book stands at ₹240 billion with EVs accounting for 64% and Robotics and Physical AI at 3%
items.quote: at the end of Q1 FY27, our net order book stands at 240 billion, with EVs accounting for 64%.

items.statement: Robotics and Physical AI order book totals ₹8 billion including three secured orders worth ₹6 billion
items.quote: Together, these three orders, they add ₹6 billion to our Robotics and Physical AI orderbook, which takes the total order book for Sona Comstar – Q1 FY27 Earnings Call this new vertical to ₹ 8 billion

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 23.1%, down 0.7% year-on-year due to input cost inflation, labor cost increases, pass-through timing gap, and product mix impact from traction motor sales
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 23.1%, which is lower by about 0.7% compared to the same quarter last year. The margin was lower primarily on account of product mix and higher input prices, despite the positive impact of the operating leverage.

items.statement: Expect recovery measures to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27 onwards as material costs pass through and cost reduction measures catch up
items.quote: We expect that these recovery measures will become progressively more visible from quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Demand remained healthy across all markets; India strong in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers, Europe growing, US improved meaningfully, China mixed but fastest growing geography due to suspension motor ramp-up
items.quote: Demand has remained healthy across all the markets we serve. India delivered another strong quarter, particularly in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers, which was phenomenal. Europe has been, surprisingly to many, it has not just remained stable, it's actually growing now. And the US has also improved meaningfully, as the quarter has progressed.

items.statement: BEV revenue grew 107% year-on-year to ₹436 crore, constituting 44% of automotive product sales, with EV order book at 69 programs across 36 customers
items.quote: BEV revenue grew by 107% to 436 crores over the same quarter last year. BEV revenue constituted 44% of our automotive product sales.

items.statement: Invested around ₹2,750 crores across acquisitions of Comstar, Noveliс, and Railway Business over last 7 years; these contribute roughly 40% of revenue and ~₹270 crore net annual profit
items.quote: Over the last 7 years, we've invested around 2 ,750 crores across the acquisitions of Comstar, Noveli c, and the Railway Business. And today at the end of Q1, these 3 businesses contribute roughly 40% of our revenue.

items.statement: Inflation remains biggest near-term challenge with elevated commodity and input costs impacting margins; April was tough, May tougher, June showed improvement as pass-throughs and cost reductions caught up
items.quote: Inflation continues to be the biggest near -term challenge. Commodities and other input costs remain elevated. They have impacted margins during the quarter. April was tough, Sona Comstar – Q1 FY27 Earnings Call May was even tougher, but June showed

items.statement: Announced strategic partnership with DENSO via two joint ventures: JV1 for high voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems (4+ wheel) with DENSO majority stake; JV2 for 2/3 wheelers with Sona Comstar majority ownership and reciprocal ro
items.quote: Yesterday, we announced what I believe is the most important strategic partnership in Sona Comstar's history. A partnership with DENSO.

items.statement: Robotics order book of Rs 800 crore with SOPs starting as early as this quarter and most within 12-15 months
items.quote: They range, some of them are as early as next quarter, some of them next year, but they are not very far in the future. Let's put it that way.

items.statement: Most robotics orders will start production within 12 to 15 months, with one starting this quarter and one next quarter
items.quote: most of this will start production, let's say within 12 to 15 months Sona Comstar – Q1 FY27 Earnings Call max. I mean, like Vivek said, one will probably start within a quarter or so, and, the rest probably in a year or so

items.statement: One robotics order SOP this quarter, one next quarter, one within 15 months
items.quote: Actually, 1 is this quarter, 1 is next quarter, 1 within 15 months.

items.statement: High voltage motor market size estimated at Rs 24,000 crore by 2030, potentially 3x by 2035
items.quote: Market size, I did say 2030, 24,000 crores, but if you were to look at 2035, this number will be many times that. It will be maybe 3 times that, and that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Capex intensity for high voltage motor and control systems is low: Rs 1 capex yields Rs 11-12 revenue
items.quote: It will be at least 11-12

items.statement: EV demand is strong; company not constrained by demand but by OEM supply chain bottlenecks
items.quote: EV is in a way, right now, we are not constrained by demand. Actually, all our OEMs are not constrained by demand. They are constrained by their own supply chain challenges.

items.statement: India is the fastest growing EV market globally; Europe electrifying fast; US shifting to hybrids
items.quote: India is actually the fastest growing EV market in the world, I think, right now. So India is doing phenomenally well. USA, we are seeing a shift to hybrids as you saw even in one of our events, but the EV market is not doing so well in the US right now.

items.statement: Suspension motors growing fastest among existing products; traction motors second fastest
items.quote: I think suspension motors are growing the fastest rate. The traction motor would be the second.

items.statement: VA per employee declined due to product mix shift toward assembly-heavy motor and railway businesses
items.quote: So while the higher the better is, is obviously the rule, but the thing is that 4.5 times, itself is also very strong. So I'm not tr ying to take away the fact that it has come down, but basically, it can vary from quarter to quarter

items.statement: Rare earth magnet restrictions persist; company uses light rare earth alternatives with no shortage impact
items.quote: Yeah, rare earth magnets are still restricted. So heavy rare earth magnets cannot be imported. Almost all that we do today is with light rare earth alternatives, and it's working fine.

items.statement: New product ramp timeline: years 1-3 no revenue, year 4 first revenue, year 5 $10M, year 7-8 $100M; robotics expected faster
items.quote: First 3 years when you make a new product or get into a new technology, you make no money. Year 4, you see your 1st $1 of revenue. Year 5, you start making the 1st $10 million odd dollar number, and year 7 or year 8 is when it becomes a $100 million business.

items.statement: JV1 (2W/3W traction motors) leads JV2 (high voltage); JV1 to kickstart faster
items.quote: The first, JV will be leading it and the 2nd JV will be following it, so I can't share you the timing exactly. But, the first JV is the one which will kickstart, faster.

items.statement: JV2 to begin with India market, then expand globally in phase two
items.quote: We begin with India and then we look at the world. I think it is also in, Maebara San from Denso has answered even in the press release, I think there is a mention that in time, in phase two is when we would look at it.

items.statement: Robotics product lifecycle shorter than automotive; generations change more frequently
items.quote: I think unlike automotive, this generation changes will happen more frequently. Vivek Vikram Singh: Correct. Vikram Verma: So even the largest guys, has already started making the 3rd generation. The 1st generation has not come on the

items.statement: Company has sufficient capacity for EV growth; built capacity ahead of markets
items.quote: We have always built capacity ahead of markets and that is definitely not our problem, but unfortunately, Nitin, and Sona Comstar – Q1 FY27 Earnings Call as you well understand, any vehicle has hundreds of parts

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 5 years for both top and bottom line
items.quote: we can grow in the range of 15% to 20% CAGR. So 1 year can be here and there because of XYZ reasons. But the way India demand is growing and the plant that the capacities that we have, eventually plant will ramp up and we can have a CAGR growth of 15% to 20% for the next 5 years.

items.statement: Board approved INR600 crore capex for Epoxy Resin & Formulations (125,000 TPA) and Multipurpose Plant
items.quote: I'm also pleased to announce that our Board has approved a strategic capex plan for 2 new projects. We are entering into the Epoxy Resin & Formulations with a capacity of 125,000 tons per annum and setting up a multipurpose plant.

items.statement: Targets INR500 crore revenue from Multipurpose Plant (chlorotoluenes & ECH derivatives) by FY29-FY30
items.quote: our target is to reach -- once the multipurpose plant will be commissioned, our target is to reach all the derivatives, specialty product portfolio, which we are producing in multipurpose plant, along with the chlorotoluene derivatives, we wanted to close to around INR500 crores revenue we would like to target.

items.statement: Chlorotoluenes + MPP combined EBITDA margin estimated at 22-23% at peak utilization
items.quote: So the estimated margin would be in the range of 22%, 23% kind of thing. And again, once we commission the plant, it will take time to ramp up, maybe 1.5 or 2 years' time to reach the optimum level utilization levels.

items.statement: No further captive power investment; energy needs to be met via solar-wind hybrid PPAs (40 MW contracted, more to come)
items.quote: We are not going to invest further in the captive power plant. Whatever we are going further, the energy requirement is going to be catered from solar and wind hybrid agreement, which we are doing with the different suppliers on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Caustic soda utilization ~75% due to short-term oversupply; long-term demand supported by alumina expansion and downstream growth
items.quote: caustic, I believe because of the way the alumina expansion is happening in the country. So, we believe we are going to be net import of caustic continuously in India, irrespective of the capacity addition will happen gradually.

items.statement: KFC store expansion guidance of 60 to 80 stores for the year remains unchanged
items.quote: The earlier guidance for KFC in terms of 60 to 80 stores in a year remains the same. That continues. No change in that particular guidance.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store expansion will remain cautious for calendar year 2026
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, we have called out that we will be quite cautious in terms of store expansion. That w as the case for calendar year '25. That will remain the case for even calendar year '26

items.statement: Sri Lanka store opening guidance remains unchanged despite profitability challenges
items.quote: So the guidance remains for this particular year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG guidance remains high single digit
items.quote: On Sri Lanka, the guidance, we should be in that same region. Sanjay Purohit: High single digit

items.statement: New store expansion decisions based on internal strike rate metrics and payback thresholds
items.quote: Our new store expansion is based on the metrics or strike rates, which we track internally. One is, whenever we launch x number of stores in a year, at the end of one year, what level of ADS we are delivering and what the strike rates are compared to what we have taken in payback.

items.statement: Total restaurant count reached 1,074 as of June 30, 2026 with 22 new stores added in Q1
items.quote: We added sixteen KFC restaurants, five Pizza Hut in India, one Pizza Hut in Sri Lanka. Our total restaurant count was 1,074 as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin improved 120 bps to 16.9% despite energy cost pressures
items.quote: This, combined with improved dine-in and takeaway mix, better operating leverage meant that the restaurant EBITDA improved by 120 basis points over last year. And this is despite the challenges in terms of the pricing pressures which we faced on the energy cost, especially in the terms of gas cost. The overall restaurant EBITDA came at very healthy 16.9%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA margin declined 110 bps to -3.6% due to higher energy costs
items.quote: However, higher energy cost impacted the restaurant EBITDA, which came at loss of 3.6%, down by 110 basis points.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin at 8.4%, up from prior year
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA came in at INR75 crores, up 37% year-on-year and margin was 8.4%.

items.statement: KFC took 2% price increase during Q1 FY27 in two instalments
items.quote: This was a combination of lower discounts compared to last year as well as price increase of 2% during the quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut took 2% price increase towards end of Q1 FY27 in two instalments
items.quote: Gross margin improved by 80 basis points, again, here as well on the basis of lower discounts and a price increase of 2% taken towards the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Price hikes restricted to 50-60% of inflation, balance managed through supply chain efficiencies
items.quote: We have always called out that we never take price hikes exactly same as inflation. So we would typically restrict our price hikes to 50% to 60% of the inflation, and the rest of the impact we would try and manage through efficiencies on our supply chain and efficiencies through other lines on the P&L.

items.statement: Demand environment remains similar with no material improvement; KFC SSSG driven by company actions
items.quote: I don't think there's been any material improvement in the demand environment. I would say it has remained similar. Some of the upside at KFC, that we are seeing is as a direct outcome of the work that we have done to improve sales.

items.statement: Month-on-month trends volatile: April-May good, June weak, July good due to Shravan timing shift
items.quote: April, May were good. June was not so good. July is good because of the difference of Shravan starting in North, earlier last year to this year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka profitability normalization expected to take at least a couple of quarters
items.quote: At least a couple of quarters away.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.3%, within guided framework; normalized margins in line with long-term 20% expectation
items.quote: Q1 EBITDA was INR1,032 million. It was up 8.5% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter at a margin of 18.3%, which is within the framework that we had guided for Q1 when we met last.

items.statement: Organic constant currency growth 5% YoY excluding RECO contract; overall constant currency growth 11.4% YoY and 2.9% QoQ
items.quote: Normalizing for that, our overall constant currency growth for Q1 FY27 came in at 18% and the organic constant currency growth is 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Revenue visibility improved to USD462 million, up 19% YoY; signed 3 new long-term annuity contracts, total annuity clients now 113
items.quote: Our contract pipeline continues to be strong. The revenue visibility improved to USD462 million. It was up 19% year-on-year from USD388 million a year ago.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions; significant capital allocation to AI infrastructure build-out; consistent dividend policy maintained
items.quote: A, we are actively looking at acquisitions. Second, as we have mentioned in the past and I mentioned earlier, we have a significant investment going into AI and AI-related build-out of infrastructure. So those are two significant areas that will consume capital.

items.statement: SweetRush phased margin buildup impacting near-term margins; AI investments continuing but returns becoming more material
items.quote: The year-on-year margin movement reflects the phased margin buildup of SweetRush together with the continued investment in AI as well as the sunsetting of the North American real estate contract.

items.statement: Target to achieve 25% blended EBITDA margin over next few years
items.quote: So, the target for the company overall is to achieve an EBITDA margin of 25% in the next few years, and we are right now on track to achieve that.

items.statement: Budgeted INR48 crores capex to expand skid assembly capacity from 2,000 to 15,000 units per annum
items.quote: And for that, we have budgeted the capex of INR48 crores. So, the entire capex would be utilized to increase the capacity from 2,000 to 15,000.

items.statement: Budgeted INR54 crores capex to expand flexible hose capacity from 16.5 to 20 million meters per annum, completion by Q3 FY27
items.quote: And the budgeted capex for the same for the entire was around INR54 crores. The plan -- so some of it was spent in FY25, some of it was spent in FY26 and now the remaining would be completed in FY27.

items.statement: Receive tentative dispatch schedule 2 months in advance; Q2 delivery schedule available but not shared publicly
items.quote: So, we generally receive the tentative dispatch schedule from our customer 2 months in advance with regards to the tentative dispatch that they plan, for which the designs are in the final stages of approval.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 468 bps YoY to 23.04%; PAT margin near 13%
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR33.5 crores, which is up by 116% on a year-on-year basis with margins expanding by 468 basis points as compared to the same quarter in last year to 23.04%.

items.statement: Flexible hose margins 16-20%, assemblies 22-26%; blended around 22-23% this quarter
items.quote: So, when we sell the flexible hose just in the hose form, margins range between 16% to 20%. And when we sell the assemblies, the margins range anywhere between 22% to 26% margins.

items.statement: Fire hose assembly margins range 23-26%
items.quote: The fire hose assemblies has margins ranging between 23% to 26%.

items.statement: Expect international skid assembly business this financial year; international potential multifold vs India
items.quote: Yes. So, we are definitely on track. And in this financial year, we'll definitely have business coming in from international market.

items.statement: Skid assemblies contributed INR32.4 crores (23% of revenue) in Q1 FY27; volume 1,040 units
items.quote: Revenue from SFN Skid Assemblies reached INR32.4 crores in this quarter, which is contributing to approximately 23% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Flexible hose assembly split: 63% assemblies/fittings, 37% plain hose in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In this quarter, approximately 66% of the business was through -- 63% of the business was selling of the fittings and assembly products and about 37% of the business was selling the flexible hose, so 63% and 37%, yes.

items.statement: Skid capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/annum; target 15,000 by Q3 FY27
items.quote: As part of our capital expenditure plans, we have expanded the capacity of skid assemblies from 6,000 units to 9,000 units per annum. And we further -- and we have the plan to further increase it to 15,000 units per annum

items.statement: Flexible hose capacity expansion from 17.5 to 20 million meters/annum to complete by Q3 FY27
items.quote: On the flexible hoses vertical, we have planned to increase the production from 17.5 million meters per annum currently to 20 million meters per annum and it should be completed by Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Flexible hose segment peak revenue potential INR650-675 crores at 70% assembly mix and peak utilization
items.quote: With the -- at the peak utilization and assuming that 70% of the sales comes in from the assemblies, we are looking at a top line of anywhere between INR650 crores to INR675 crores.

items.statement: Logistics costs increased significantly in Q1 due to West Asia crisis impacting margins sequentially
items.quote: Also to add to that, just because the -- barring the material cost in the last -- in the Q1, if you also would see that logistics cost also has increased because of the crisis that has happened in West Asia.

items.statement: About 40 skids per megawatt of liquid-cooled IT load on average
items.quote: About 40-odd skids go into 1 megawatt on an average.

items.statement: FY27 loan growth guidance of 22% and FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crores plus
items.quote: As we look forward, the momentum of the first quarter marks an important step towards Vision 2029 and making us well positioned to achieve the target FY29 loan book of INR16,000 crores plus and 22% growth in FY27.

items.statement: ROA target of 1.35-1.4% for FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE target 15% plus by FY29
items.quote: We expect further ROTA expansion and targeting to make it towards 1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29 and ROE expansion to 15% plus by FY29.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.21% in Q1 FY27 from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 driven by deposit repricing and higher CD ratio
items.quote: Net interest margin has improved to 4.21% against 4.06% in the previous quarter and 4.06% a year ago. The same is supported by a decline in the deposit cost on repricing, coupled with acceleration in the CD ratio.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 2.47% (down 28 bps YoY, 7 bps QoQ); NNPA improved to 1.14% (down from 1.24% QoQ, 1.39% YoY); PCR improved to 54.5%; SMA 1&2 at 4.78% (down from 5.47% YoY)
items.quote: Asset quality, showing consistent improvement during the quarter with gross NPA improved to 2.47%, improved by 28 basis points and by 7 basis points on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis respectively. Net NPA has also improved significantly and now stood at 1.14%.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 UTs; focus on semi-urban and rural markets
items.quote: As of June '26, our branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories, strengthening our presence in rural and semi-urban markets.

items.statement: Average CD ratio at 83% in Q1 FY27; targeting mid-to-high 80s over next 2-3 years to drive NIM expansion
items.quote: We are presently reporting an average CD ratio of 83%. And as we discussed over the last couple of calls, we intend to take it to the mid- to high 80s.

items.statement: Opex at 2.95-2.98% in Q1 FY27; expected to improve in FY27 as salary increments annualize and business scales; larger opex leverage expected in FY29
items.quote: Typically, current quarter, we're seeing at around 2.95% to 2.98% levels. That is the opex in the current quarter. I'm seeing an improvement in the coming period for this.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; capital adequacy at 21.6% provides ample headroom for growth
items.quote: Our balance sheet remained well capitalized and liquid. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 21.6%, providing sufficient headroom to support the future growth.

items.statement: Management does not provide guidance and will not change this approach.
items.quote: We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself. And as some of you have noticed in the past, occasionally with some frustration, we do not give guidance. We would rather you judge us by terms of what we do rather than what we promise.

items.statement: Core profit after tax (with DAC, without discounting and mark-to-market) fell 5% YoY to INR190 crores.
items.quote: So when we look at it from that perspective, our profit after tax with DAC, but without discounting and mark-to-market is INR190 crores compared to INR200 crores a year ago. This is a drop of 5%.

items.statement: Combined ratio (NEP with DAC) worsened to 107.2% from 104.3% with discounting.
items.quote: Combined ratio is 107.2% with DAC and 104.3% with discounting. So you can actually see the difference between the 2 numbers also is roughly about 3%.

items.statement: Loss ratio increased to 73.3% from 70.3% YoY, driven by private car own damage.
items.quote: the essential increase is happening because loss ratio has increased from 70.3% in the first quarter to 73.3%.

items.statement: Motor market share fell to 5.6% from 6.25% due to corrective actions in private car and commercial vehicles.
items.quote: our motor market share is now 5.6%. This compared to Q1 last year or compared to the whole of '25-'26 against 6.25% for the whole year.

items.statement: New business in 2-wheeler grew 26% YoY with collected premium of INR546 crores.
items.quote: New business in 2-wheeler has grown by 26% in Q1, and our collected premium is INR546 crores against INR433 crores last year, an increase of INR113 crores in premium income.

items.statement: Fire business de-grew 37% vs industry de-growth of 27-28% to protect gross loss ratios for reinsurers.
items.quote: if you look at the fire business, industry has -- if I remember, industry has de-grown by minus 27%, 28%. We have de-grown by 37%.

items.statement: Third-party loss ratio stable at 66.6%; reserving includes legal inflation and wage hikes; no separate provision for Supreme Court ruling yet.
items.quote: On the TP, our loss ratio is 66.6%, similar to what it was, broadly stable. Third party, as we have always said, is a long-tail business, and we read it on a full year basis, not any single quarter.

items.statement: Aggressive claim settlement on homemaker claims underway; conservative reserving maintained; no bet on judicial outcomes.
items.quote: We will go out and aggressively settle homemakers compromises, particularly or specifically, we anyway settle, as I gave you a number, 83% of the claims on the TP side.

items.statement: Equity allocation increased to 9.5% of AUM with INR268 crores unrealized gains; fixed income duration raised to 4.9 years.
items.quote: Now we are sitting at 9.5% in this period, and on top of it, we are sitting at an unrealized gains of INR268 crores.

items.statement: Dividend possible on IGAAP basis given 242% solvency; decision pending RBC norms and board approval in Q4.
items.quote: Based on where we are on IGAAP profitability, we can easily pay dividend because our solvency justifies it. And it will go up hopefully every quarter. By how much, we don't know. So I think all we are doing is waiting for the RBC norms to come.

items.statement: Motor TP rates unchanged for 5 years; 90-95% of vehicles need a hike; management not waiting for hike to act.
items.quote: On a thumb rule, I would say 90%, 95% of the vehicles should see a hike in TP. But the question is, should we wait for it in the hope that it will increase this month, that month or you say right now, it increase hasn't happened and we'll go and run our business on that basis.

items.statement: Gross written premium down 8% YoY; excluding reinsurance inward in health and crop, de-growth is ~2% similar to industry.
items.quote: On the gross written premium, we are down by 8%. Now most of it is actually coming in because we -- the drop in the reinsurance inward business, essentially in health and crop, so group health and crop, where pricing was unattractive.

items.statement: Solvency strong at 2.43x (IGAAP); IFRS net worth INR8,200 crores vs INR7,600 crores at March 31.
items.quote: Solvency is very strong at 2.43 times and this obviously plays in terms of the optionality we have. But there is one number here, which is actually going the other way. And that number is net earned premium.

items.statement: Long-term advance premium stands at INR3,387 crores (Motor INR2,879 crores, Non-motor INR508 crores).
items.quote: Long-term advance premium now stands at INR3,387 crores. Motor is INR2,879 crores and non-motor is INR508 crores.

items.statement: Group health loss ratio elevated due to one large bank-driven personal accident policy with high intimations.
items.quote: what happened this quarter is that we have a fairly large bank-driven personal accident policy where claims get intimated. A lot of these claims get repudiated over a period of time. So this quarter, the group level PA is essentially looking elevated because of one single large PA policy.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering 35-40% AUM growth in FY27
items.quote: Based on the strong momentum we have built, we remain confident of delivering AUM growth of 35% to 40% growth during the current financial years.

items.statement: Targeting ROA of 3.5% for FY27 driven by higher-yield product mix
items.quote: Yes. So, we are targeting around 3.5% ROA for the FY27.

items.statement: Net interest margin expected to remain in 13-14% range for FY27
items.quote: So eventually net interest margin will remain in the range of 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Planning to raise INR100 crores via preference shares by September-October 2026
items.quote: And we are in a process of raising the capital. By September or latest by October, we will raise INR100 crores to for to manage our further growth and expansion.

items.statement: Two-wheeler share to decline from 84% to 75-77% by FY27 end via personal, top-up, used 2W, 3W, SBL growth
items.quote: And we are expecting that by end of this year it should be reach around 77% to -- 75% to 77%.

items.statement: MSME LAP expected to contribute 2-3% of AUM by FY27 end
items.quote: So that loan against property we are expecting around 3% by end of -- 2% to 3% because this year only we started.

items.statement: Technology spend to remain in similar range as percentage of expenses; significant spend on personal loan software this year
items.quote: So that will -- whenever need is arising, company is spending. And as far as total percentage of the entire expense is concerned, so it will remain what we are spending today, morely in the similar range only.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing at 10.86%; Q1 increase due to holding INR200 crores liquidity
items.quote: On the funding side, our average cost of borrowing currently stands at 10.86%.

items.statement: Strong disbursement growth of 37% YoY to INR226 crores in Q1; Q2-Q3 expected to drive AUM jump due to festival season
items.quote: During the period, disbursement grew by 37% year-on-year to INR226 crores, reflecting a strong demand across the core vehicle finance portfolio and continued execution across existing market.

items.statement: Declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per equity shares on a face value of INR10 each for the financial year '26, '27, reflecting our continued commitment towards shareholders value creation.

items.statement: Battery replacement finance launched at INR60,000 ticket size for existing e-3W customers, with OEM tie-ups
items.quote: Yes. So, this is INR60,000 ticket size product. And basically after 15 months of utilization of three-wheeler, generally battery starts giving some issues and eventually the entire vehicle goes into that kind of situation where they generally, it becomes a non-performing asset.

items.statement: MSME LAP ticket size INR8-20 lakhs targeting shop-owning businessmen
items.quote: And the ticket size will be around will start from INR8 lakhs to INR20 lakhs. We are talking about the MSME LAP, right? So INR20 lakhs will be the highest loan which we are going to provide to the customers.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 130-150 crore; FY27 turnover projection INR 220-250 crore
items.quote: we are estimating to get a turnover of around INR130 crores to INR150 crores somewhere in between for this financial

items.statement: PAT margin expected at 17-18% for FY27; Q1 EBITDA margin dip due to raw material invoicing timing
items.quote: we are estimating a margin of around 17% to 18% PAT year-on-year

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin fell from 40% to 20% YoY due to raw material purchase timing shift to Q1
items.quote: Last year, most of the raw material was purchased in Q4 of the previous year. This year, most of the raw material got purchased earlier but the stock got delivered only in Q1 time

items.statement: B2B/B2C mix to remain 70/30; ticket size per school increased from INR 1 lakh to INR 40 lakh via Pelican platform
items.quote: going forward, the mix is going to be same 70%, 30% but the turnovers will increase on both fronts

items.statement: Notebook manufacturing capacity at 10-20% of addressable demand; will add machines as scale grows; textbook printing at 80-85% capacity, sufficient up to INR 300 crore turnover
items.quote: right now we have the machines what we have for notebook can only sustain like 10% to 20% of the demand of 100% of our market wherever our presence is there

items.statement: Expanding into UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam; UP seen as most meaningful; targeting market share growth from 1-2% to 5% in new states over 3 years
items.quote: in the next three years, we are estimating to grow it to 5%

items.statement: Technology (LMS/AI) bundled free with textbooks; MRP increased by INR 10-12 per book to cover server and development costs
items.quote: I increased the MRP by another INR10 to INR12 and started giving this technology for free

items.statement: Curriculum changes occur every 20-30 years (last 2020 NEP); minor annual changes managed with early publisher intimation
items.quote: post-independence the curriculum was completely revamped three times, sir, so far. The last update was in 2020 when the New Education Policy was introduced

items.statement: Textbook prescriptions lock in 3-4 year recurring revenue per school; 13,000 schools currently supplied
items.quote: usually when a book gets prescribed in the school, it -- the business lasts for three to four years in that school

items.statement: Trade receivables INR 100 crore at Q1 end; 40%+ recovered by July-August; 90% by Oct-Nov; 7-10% over 6 months
items.quote: out of the INR100 crores more than 40% has been recovered by July and August. By October-November, 90% of the receivables will be recovered

items.statement: AUM growth guidance maintained at 25-30% for FY27
items.quote: We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 3.5-4% for FY27
items.quote: Our guidance on credit cost was, and at the beginning of the year we had given a guidance of 3.5% to 4%, and this appears well within our grasp now.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 14.25-14.75% for FY27 despite Q1 beat
items.quote: From a NIM perspective, the guidance that we had given, we expect to stay on target.

items.statement: Opex ratio guidance maintained at 8.25-8.75% for FY27
items.quote: We did realize that quarter 1, quarter 2 we might be out of those bands and quarter 3, quarter 4 we will be very much in the band giving a result which for the entire year should be in that band.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 NIM improved 20bps sequentially to 15.9%
items.quote: Despite the increasing share of mortgage loans in our portfolio, our NIM actually improved by 20 basis points sequentially to 15.9%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost at 10.2%, expected to drop 10-15bps further with rating upgrade
items.quote: Our incremental borrowing has been coming at nearly 60 bps lower and therefore my cost of the incremental borrowing that I'm doing today is at around 10.20%. This we expect with the credit upgrading, we expect to drop this further by around 10 to 15 bps.

items.statement: Borrowing cost expected to reduce 20-25bps on incremental borrowings due to rating upgrade
items.quote: It is expected to, on one hand, broaden our lender relationships and enhance funding flexibility, and on the other hand, it is also going to reduce our borrowing cost by approximately 20 to 25 basis points on the incremental borrowings over the course of the year.

items.statement: Strong demand environment for working capital from micro-MSMEs continues
items.quote: We have continued to see a constructive demand environment for working capital from our core market.

items.statement: Added 44,000 new borrowers in Q1 FY27, up 38% YoY despite tighter underwriting
items.quote: During this quarter, we added more than 44,000 new borrowers, which is a growth of 38% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Mortgage share at 22% of portfolio, expected to grow marginally in FY27
items.quote: While we are today already at 22% of our portfolio in mortgages, we expect it to only grow marginally through the year.

items.statement: Long-term target: 60-70% hypothecation, 30% Micro LAP, up to 10% other products (gold/solar) in 3 years
items.quote: We will like to see 60%-70% hypothecation, 30% Micro LAP, and at best 10% can be some other product, and this is over the next 3 years I would say.

items.statement: Plan to add 40-50 branches in FY27, focusing on deepening existing markets
items.quote: This year, our strategy remains focused on deepening our presence in existing markets rather than entering new geographies, and hence we expect to add only around 40 to 50 branches during the year.

items.statement: TMD order book is 3,200 crores with 2,400 crores active orders
items.quote: With respect to the order book, currently we hold an order book of 3200 crores for TMD of which the active orders are around 2,400 crores.

items.statement: ATC order book is around 1,000 crores for execution over three to three and a half years
items.quote: The order book for ATC is in the region of thousand crores of orders for execution over a period of three years, three to three and a half years.

items.statement: TMD order book mix is 70% projects and 30% unitary machines
items.quote: For the previous question of Mr. Lakshmi Narayan, the order book would still have close to 70% of projects and 30% of unitary missions Within the order book what we mentioned.

items.statement: ATC new facility capex of 150 crores for land and building over 18-24 months
items.quote: We are going to have I think 150 crores worth of land building being built. Building basically land is of course our own. So, building being built up for ATC and this, the timeline for this is over at least 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: ATC margins higher this quarter due to favorable product mix of assemblies over components
items.quote: The margin for the current quarter has been a little bit higher considering that there was lot of the ratio the mix of products versus assembled components. There are a mix and this time there's a little bit higher sale on the assemblies rather than on the components.

items.statement: MTD margin drop due to lower turnover and operational leverage; capacity utilization at 75-80%
items.quote: See, compared to Q4, Q1 is of course slightly less in terms of turnover. But I think if you were to actually look at Q1 of last year to Q1 of this year or you can compare multiple of Q ones of the previous years, I think Machine Tool Division has done extremely well thanks to two things.

items.statement: MTD historical 12-14% EBIT margins require full capacity utilization and turnover increase; no timeline given
items.quote: So you're talking about probably on 300,400 Crores of turnover with this margin. But today we are doing much more. Varied products and much more larger cost base. Which. Which is where I said that definitely. A turnover to get turnover increase and. Utilisation of capacity will give us better numbers and we can't put a timeline on that.

items.statement: Costs up 3-3.5% due to commodities, fuel, gas, transport; working on mitigation and price pass-through
items.quote: If you want a number on that. It could be anywhere up from between three to three and a half percent where the costs would have, would be going up.

items.statement: Price revisions done across divisions; ATC and Foundry have contractual price revision clauses
items.quote: We have to pass on It happens in multiple divisions. For example, in divisions like ATC Foundry, we have a clear clause with the customer for revision of price. So we do that constantly.

items.statement: Textile demand outlook positive due to state policies (Gujarat, Odisha, MP), FTAs, and modernization needs
items.quote: There are a lot of state policies which have come. Gujarat, Orissa and I think Madhya Pradesh. There's a specific region, Dhar region, I think, I think that is these are the policies which are kind of triggering a lot of activity within the order book. And, for new order book.

items.statement: Textile capacity utilization around 60%; gradual increase in spindle absorption expected
items.quote: Textile utilization still hovers around 60 percent. As far as textile utilization is concerned with respect to margins on m achine tool business the product mix is one of the key things

items.statement: ATC revenue split 90% export/10% domestic; composite 20%/metallics 80% of turnover; order book 25% composite/75% metallics
items.quote: To the split it is still 90 -10. That is 90% export and what do you call ten 10% domestic composite metallics. It is around just one second. Yeah, 20% within this turnover 20% is composite and 80% is Metallics portion of it.

items.statement: Middle East tensions increasing commodity, fuel, gas, transport costs; supply chain resilience focus with 4-5 month material visibility
items.quote: All the costs, be it commodity, be it fuel, be it the gas and. A lot of these are being used. So, if you look at LPG, if you look at our sheet metal process, we use helium. If you look at So transport costs are up, commodity cost is up, everything is up to some extent.

items.statement: Auto winder feedback good; booking more orders for rollout in last quarter of FY27
items.quote: With respect to auto winder, yes, we have supplied them in the south, the feedback is good. We will be booking orders closer to the last quarter of this year. More orders for more rollouts.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 15.46%, up 1050 bps YoY and 400 bps QoQ, driven by volume growth, pricing actions, inventory gains, and renewable power.
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved significantly to 15.46%, representing an expansion of 1050 basis points year-on-year and 400 basis points over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Capex of over Rs 100 crore planned for FY27, focused on mother yarn capacity (commissioning FY28), value-added filament yarn products, renewable power at Bharuch, efficiency upgrades, and safety improvements.
items.quote: We expect to spend over 100 crores in CAPEX in the current year, current financial year.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; capex funded internally; healthy cash balance on balance sheet noted by analyst.
items.quote: One more question is about the healthy cash balance, which is there on the balance sheet. So, my question is regarding, if you could talk about the CAPEX plans for the company...

items.statement: Expects full-year performance to be 4.5x to 5x Q1 results
items.quote: So typically, we see that the first quarter by the end of the year, it is not just multiplied by 4, but sometimes it is more like 4.5x to 5x that you will see at the end of the year. And that's what we are expecting this year also.

items.statement: Spent INR 5,300 crores in Q1; full-year capex plan of INR 25,000 crores with 50% for renewables
items.quote: On the capital expenditure, for the first time, we spent INR 5,300 crores in the first quarter. And we expect that the INR 25,000 crores that we have lined up for this year, we'll be able to implement.

items.statement: Q2 capex expected to be higher than INR 6,000 crores, possibly closer to INR 6,500 crores
items.quote: you can assume in our quarter 2 also, we're kind of looking at a capex plan of probably higher than INR 6,000 crores. Maybe if everything goes well, it will be closer to INR 6,500 crores.

items.statement: Renewable capacity to increase from 6.7 GW to over 9 GW by end of FY27 with 2.5-2.7 GW addition
items.quote: Right now, we are at 6.7 gigawatts. We add 2.5 gigawatts. We'll cross 9 gigawatts by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Rooftop business plans to grow 60-70% this year after 100% growth last year
items.quote: In fact, last year, we grew by 100%, and this year also, we have plans to grow by about 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Module plant crossed 1,000 MW production in Q1; cell production catching up
items.quote: For the first time, our module plant we crossed 1,000 megawatt in the first quarter, and we expect that we have virtually peaked over there or peaking over there in terms of our module production.

items.statement: Power demand grew 8.5% in Q1 with May at 11% and June at 9.8%; July consistently 260-270 GW
items.quote: The power demand growth has been very strong in the first quarter. It was nearly 8.5% increase. In fact, in the month of May, it was nearly 11% and June was 9.8%.

items.statement: Industry-wide renewable curtailment around 5% in Q1; expected to settle in next few quarters as transmission lines progress
items.quote: there's been a general curtailment of roughly about 5%. And that we think is also the industry trend. But given that a lot of transmission lines and evacuation lines are in fast progression, we think that this curtailment will settle in, in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Indonesian coal prices up 5-7%; expect up to 5% increase over next 9 months; no major impact from new export regulations
items.quote: I would say about 5% to 7%. So in that range, the coal price increase. And we don't expect too much of changes happening. But yes, up to 5% over the next 9 months, you can expect.

items.statement: Pumped hydro project (1,000 MW) to start commissioning from calendar year 2029 with 3 units at 2-month gaps
items.quote: We are doing very good construction work over there. And we expect that beginning of calendar year 2029, we will be in a position to commission the plant. And since there are 3 units, they will get commissioned with a gap of 2 months for each unit.

items.statement: TBCB projects Jalpura-Khurja line to complete in days; Bikaner-Neemrana line by October; revenues to flow from Q2 onwards
items.quote: One will get completed, the Jalpura -Khurja line in the next few days. The other one, the Bikaner -Neemrana line will also get commissioned by October. So again, huge pipeline of projects, and you will see the benefits of that accruing in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Mumbai transmission regulated investment pipeline of INR 10,000 crores over next 5 years with efficiency upsides
items.quote: we have a huge pipeline of investment, which is there in Mumbai transmission, nearly INR 10,000 crores of investment will happen in the next 5 years. And this is on a regulated basis. So we not only get the regulated, but also certain upsides because of better performance on the efficiency and availability of this transmission system.

items.statement: Net debt to underlying EBITDA at 3.41 and net debt to equity at 1.25; within self-set guardrails for investment
items.quote: Our net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41 and our net debt to equity is 1.25. This is within the guardrails that we have set for ourselves for the investment.

items.statement: Tata Projects legacy losses narrowing; only 10% of legacy projects remain; expect turnaround after one more quarter
items.quote: We are at something like just 10% of the legacy projects in last stage there and cost to correction takes place because of that reason. And you will find that possibly maybe one more quarter will have an impact on Tata Projects.

items.statement: Rooftop realization varies by module type and scheme (ULA vs commercial); mix impact explains billing vs order inflow difference
items.quote: One is different places. So 1 kilowatt, we supply a large quantity under the ULA scheme of the government. So that's a different type of modules. Then you have other places where you supply a higher capacity, different modules.

items.statement: Bhutan Khorlochhu 600 MW hydro project PPA signed with UPPCL and regulatory approval received; expected operational by CY2030
items.quote: We have also tied up the PPA for 600 megawatt of Bhutan project, the Khorlochhu project with UPPCL. And the PPA has been signed with them, and it has got the regulatory approval.

items.statement: Management expects normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores per year but will consider good opportunities with reasonable returns
items.quote: So I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at. But having said that, if there are good opportunities and there are any reasonable return projects coming, we'll not be opposed to look at that.

items.statement: Granulation project on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Granulation project is progressing well - as planned, we are on track for commissioning this in Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Capacity expansion of key molecules in Crop Protection expected to be commissioned by September
items.quote: Capacity expansion of key molecules is on track and is expected to be commissioned by September, strengthening our ability to support future growth.

items.statement: Evaluating SSP facility at Senegal costing $5-6 million for 100,000-150,000 tons capacity
items.quote: Besides that, we wanted to invest in a single super phosphate facility, it doesn't cost much maybe $5 million to 6 million to create 100,000 - 150,000 tons of SSP.

items.statement: Fertilizer business margins under pressure due to elevated ammonia and sulphur prices not factored in subsidy rates
items.quote: Fertilizer business margins were under pressure due to sudden spurt in key input raw materials like ammonia and sulphur. These prices were not factored in the subsidy rates announced by the government.

items.statement: Crop Protection EBIT increased 44% to INR159 crores on improved product mix and ability to pass on higher raw material costs in export market
items.quote: Revenue grew by 20% year -on-year to INR870 crores, while EBIT increased 44% to INR159 crores, reflecting improved product mix, traction for its key molecules and the ability to pass on higher raw material costs in the export market.

items.statement: NACL EBITDA margin improved to 11% from 8%, in line with acquisition expectations
items.quote: Our subsidiary, NACL Industries improved its performance and EBITDA has moved up by 9% to INR41 crores with margin improving to 11% from 8%. These are in line with what we envisaged at the time of acquisition.

items.statement: Specialty Nutrients business growing top line 25-30% with EBITDA margin of 20%
items.quote: We have been continuously growing the top line of Specialty Nutrient business by 25%-30% with EBITDA margin of 20%.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid prices for Q2 settled at $1,700 vs $1,360 in Q1, reflecting sharp increase
items.quote: As you are aware, phosphoric acid prices for Q 2 has been settled at $1,700 as compared to $1,360 prevailed in Q1, reflecting a sharp increase in line with the increase in international price of DAP and other raw material inputs.

items.statement: Sulphur prices holding high due to structural demand shifts from EV batteries, expected to remain high for some time but not sustainable
items.quote: Sulphur is actually against our initial expectation - sulphur is holding high. I think sulphur is likely to remain high for some time, but it's not sustainable.

items.statement: Fertilizer sales volumes moderated 9% to 10 lakh tons but market share increased to 22% from 18%
items.quote: In terms of sales, these are all early part of the season. Volumes have been moderated by 9% to 10 lakh tons as compared to corresponding period last year. Despite this, the company has strengthened its market position, increasing the primary market share to 22% compared to 18% in the last year.

items.statement: Crop Protection domestic formulation demand softer due to delayed sowings, but export markets showing improvement
items.quote: On the crop protection sector, domestic market was muted. It's the early part of the kharif season. Demand was impacted due to delay in crop s owings. However, the export markets have shown improvement, although the market remains cautious and is waiting for price stabilization

items.statement: SSP volumes grew 19% with differentiated products GroPlus and Urea-SSP constituting over 50% of SSP sales
items.quote: SSP business continued its strong growth trajectory with volumes increasing by 19% - we have been focusing on differentiated products like GroPlus and Urea-SSP, which constituted more than 50% of the total SSP sales, highlighting the success of company's strategy to drive premiumization and improve product mix.

items.statement: Government subsidy rates for NP/NPK do not fully compensate for post-Middle East crisis raw material cost increases; industry engaging for review
items.quote: On the subsidy front, the government announced increase of about 10% in subsidy rates across Nitrogen, Phosphatic and Sulphur nutrients under the NBS regime. This rate has been announced without factoring the Middle East crisis situation. These rates do not fully compensate for the increase in global raw material costs, which happened subsequent to Middle East crisis.

items.statement: Ban on nano fertilizers in UP and Maharashtra moderating Nano DAP growth despite good farmer response
items.quote: There has been a ban on some of these products from fertilizer companies in the state of UP and Maharashtra, which moderated the growth.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth to track market growth of 4-5% and does not expect 23% revenue growth to continue every quarter

items.statement: Volume growth high single-digit (~9%); no specific revenue run-rate guidance; land monetization not disclosed; no inorganic acquisition plans currently

items.quote: It ranges for different products, and it ranges anywhere between 80% to 90% for different product categories across the division. Chaitanya Desai: And as you know, we are doing a fair amount of capex. So we are building our capacity for the growth

items.quote: EBITDA post open ForEx came in at INR194 crores, which is up 36.7%. The EBITDA margin has come in at 10.6% in Q1, which is up by 60 basis points over a year ago.

items.quote: Working capital is in the range of 45 to 50 days. That has been fairly constant over the period. Kushal Desai: In fact, in this quarter, we have actually improved our working capital number of days, debtors and inventory in the conductor division compared to what it was previously

items.quote: There is a possibility because of the RBI forex window that in another -- for another 5 years that ECB loans will be higher, maybe it may go from 10% to 20% of the total portfolio.
