So peak demand was almost about 271 gigawatt in the month of May and even in the month of July it almost touched about 271 gigawatt with about 12% increase in peak demand and 8% to 9% increase in energy consumption.

items.statement: Filed applications with CERC for Green RTM, Peak Power Contracts for DAM/RTM, and extending Term Ahead Market contracts from 3 to 11 months
items.quote: We have already filed an application with the CERC for approval of Green RTM Market, Peak Power Contracts for DAM and RTM, and also for enhancing the Term Ahead Market contracts from 3 months to 11 months.

items.statement: CERC discussion paper proposes reducing RTM bidding window from 15 to 5 minutes and gate closure from 75 to 50 minutes
items.quote: The paper proposes reduction of RTM auction window from 15 minutes to 5 minutes. Today, for submission of bid s in the RTM segment, a 15-minute window is provided. They are proposing to reduce it to 5 minutes and thereby reducing the gate closure time from 75 minutes to 50 minutes

items.statement: IGX traded 76.8 million MMBtu gas in FY26, profit Rs 42 crore, up 28% YoY; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu, profit Rs 16 crore
items.quote: In this last year, they did a volume of almost about 76.8 million MMBtu of gas with a profit of 42 crore rupees and with a growth of 28% on a year-on-year basis. In this quarter also, they have achieved a trade of 27.5 million MMBtu of gas with profit of 16 crore rupees.

items.statement: ICX (I-REC issuer) registered 200% growth in issuance last year; time-stamping of certificates expected to deepen market
items.quote: You can see 200% growth 7 that we have registered last year. Couple of things which are happening here which we would be dealing with in the subsequent slide which makes it quite a promising segment going forward

items.statement: Regional transmission capacity tripled in last 10-12 years to 120 GW; set to grow to 168 GW by FY32
items.quote: Today it is at 120 gigawatt. It is set to grow to 168 gigawatt by FY32 and these numbers are remarkable, very good numbers.

items.statement: Regulators pushing demand shifting via Time-of-Day tariffs with 20% daytime rebates; 50 GW additional shifting potential estimated by FY35.
items.quote: Regulators today are pushing for demand shifting. We have seen in case of Maharashtra, TOD (Time of Day) tariff more than 20% rebate has been given if you are buying during the daytime.

items.statement: Peak demand shifting from evening to daytime; 3 PM peak observed in 2026 vs evening peak in 2019 due to solar generation and agriculture load shifting.
items.quote: you can see in the evening peak demand was there but if you see now which is 2026 peak demand is somewhere near 3 pm when the solar generation is there.

items.statement: 80 GW thermal capacity addition in pipeline: 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW contracts awarded, 16 GW under planning; majority coming FY31-33.
items.quote: on the thermal side also 80 gigawatt of capacity addition is in the pipeline and 41 gigawatt is already under construction where PPAs have been signed.

items.statement: BESS arbitrage opportunity: buy at below Rs 2/day, sell at Rs 10/evening peak; FY26 average arbitrage Rs 4.81/cycle, 545 cycles possible; 2-cycle operation cost below Rs 3.5.
items.quote: For every cycle, arbitrage available in FY'26 was 4.81 rupees. Similarly, it was 5.03 rupees in FY'25 and 3.80 rupees in FY'24.

items.statement: Merchant BESS capacity growing: ACME 3,200 MWh, Juniper 500 MWh, Adani 3,400 MWh commissioned on standalone merchant basis; VGF scheme >Rs 9,000 crore support.
items.quote: ACME has started commission ing 3,200 M wH which is standalone merchant basis, Juniper has done 500 MwH again on a standalone merchant bases and Adani has done 3,400 MwH which are again on a merchant basis

items.statement: FDRE tenders emerging: prices >Rs 4-6/unit vs usual Rs 2.6-2.7; developers create 40-50% surplus capacity sold on exchange.
items.quote: It would be more than 4, 5, 6 rupees depending on your profile, depending on the conditions of the tender. But this again is one segment which is happening in a big way.

items.statement: CfD pilot launched by SECI for 500 MW peak power (not solar); VPPAs with C&I consumers selling green attributes, power on exchange; both models bring generation to market.
items.quote: Very recently one development has happened where SECI has come out with a pilot project where 500 megawatt of CfD based contract will be created.

items.statement: New products filed with CERC: Green RTM and HP-RTM (order reserved), Peak contracts (order reserved), 11-month Long Duration DEEP (currently limited to 3 months).
items.quote: Green RTM and HP-RTM, we have identified that. Some of the green power is being traded under RTM segment and when it is traded there, neither buyer nor seller is getting any advantage of the green attribute.

items.statement: LPSC rule driving volume: 8 BU cleared in FY26 (10x bid volume); Q1 FY27 already 3 BU from Central Generating Stations; IPPs and State Gencos to join.
items.quote: In the first quarter (Q1 FY'27) with the same Central Generating Stations we have done 3 billion units.

items.statement: Carbon trading expected to start in FY27.
items.quote: carbon trading is something which is again in the pipeline and we expect that in FY'27 itself we should start trading in it.

items.statement: Market coupling challenged: CERC July 2025 order for Jan 2026 implementation; IEX appealed to APTEL (Feb 2026 order: IEX not aggrieved); Supreme Court petition admitted, hearing July 27.
items.quote: Our case petition has been admitted, notice has been served and one hearing happened where the notice was served, and now on Monday (27th July) there is the second hearing.

items.statement: Grid India raised serious concerns on draft PMR: scope unclear (DAM vs I-DAM), need industry-grade software, single point of failure if Grid India is MCO, steering committee needed, inter-exchange settlement requires regulation.
items.quote: Grid India themselves have raised certain points and these are very serious points which I thought I will share with you.

items.statement: IGX filed DRHP for listing; volume 76.8 MMBtu, profit Rs 42 cr, 40%+ CAGR over 5-6 years.
items.quote: it reached with CAGR growth of over 40% a volume of 76.8 million MMBtu and reported profit of 42 crores.

items.statement: Coal Exchange incorporated June 2025; targeting 100 MT initial year volume; spot market potential 250 MT by 2035 as demand grows to 2,000 MT and commercial production to 500 MT.
items.quote: we are expecting the demand for coal to increase significantly from 1 ,200 (MT) presently to around 2 ,000 million ton nes by 2035 and we are expecting an increase in the capacity of commercial coal production to around 500 million to nnes by

items.statement: Technology adoption: >70% I-DAM cleared volume via bidding API; >50% via post-trade API; payouts to sellers by 11 AM next clearing day (Rs 40,000+ cr processed).
items.quote: Last year, we processed more than 40,000 crores into seller accounts and all within this SLA of having the payment credited into seller's account by 11am on the next clearing day of delivery.

items.statement: AI solutions launching: AI Bidding Assistance for Discoms, Auto-Bidding for C&I, AI chatbot for market data this quarter; internal AI for cybersecurity, software dev, RPA automation.
items.quote: There is an AI-powered chatbot for market data that we have already developed and in this quarter itself will do the launch of this AI Power chatbot for the entire sector.

items.statement: RTM volume expected to grow at 25-30% CAGR going forward
items.quote: I believe that RTM volume will be higher than the Day Ahead Market volume in time to come because RTM is one market where everybody is participating.

items.statement: Exchange share of total generation could reach ~25% in next 5-6 years
items.quote: We did some estimation on this and what we feel is that almost about 25 percent of the total generation that is the market size, opportunity size, maybe in the next five, six years, it can be that kind of opportunity.

items.statement: BESS two-cycle arbitrage opportunity seen for next 3-5 years
items.quote: So, we feel that for another 3-5 years, this opportunity should be there.

items.statement: Considering BESS asset investment as inorganic opportunity
items.quote: Finally, the BESS opportunity (asset), which we are considering also for us to have some play there as well.

items.statement: Coal exchange market size currently 120 MT, expected 250-300 MT by 2035
items.quote: Today, the volume transacted through the e-auction and the marketplace is almost about 120 million ton nes. Coal India alone did e-auctions of about 90 million tonnes of coal. So, the market size as on date is 120 million ton nes, and it can increase to almost about 250 -300 million tonnes by 2035

items.statement: Asset-light high-margin platform business with strong cash flows
items.quote: This (IEX) is an asset light high-margin platform business. We have strong cash-flows which will help us grow, which will help us diversify moving into inorganic territories.

items.statement: Exchange fees will be higher than MSTC/Mjunction fixed auction fees
items.quote: The fees in case of exchanges will be definitely higher than what MSTC and Mjunction are charging.

items.statement: Power demand boom driven by electrification, data centers, EVs, ACs; per capita consumption seen 1.5x by 2032
items.quote: We are banking on the (power) demand boom in the country, electrification is happening, data centers, EV, air conditioners are going to drive the demand. If it is (per capita electricity consumption) going to be 1.5X by 2032, we will have our play here.

items.statement: BESS arbitrage, capacity market, CFDs, ancillary, carbon markets identified as key new product opportunities
items.quote: BESS price arbitrage is a huge opportunity. It stands out apart from other things because other things have been there for quite some time but something like BESS arbitrage, something like capacity market, CFDs, ancillary carbon markets are which stands out where we are super bullish.

items.statement: Market coupling implementation will take long time; no timeline given; Grid India concerns noted
items.quote: It will be difficult for me to give any timeline on this, I can only tell you one thing that sometime in 1994-95 when availability-based tariff was first discussed in the country. It was finally implemented in 2003. It took so much of time. This may not take that long, but then definitely it will take a long time.

items.statement: Long-duration contracts (up to 11 months) approval delayed over 2 years; no visibility on timeline
items.quote: It's been more than two years since we have applied for that. You are right.

items.statement: MCO cost allocation, fee impact, and market share effects unresolved; to be addressed in final regulations
items.quote: I think these are the issues which are flagged by the Grid India also in their comments to CERC and in addition to the point raised by you, there are many more issues, which needs to be answered.

items.statement: Coal exchange shareholding cap 25% for any entity, 5% for trading members, similar to power/gas exchanges
items.quote: Nobody can hold more than 25 percent, and no trading member can hold more than 5%. It is similar kind of shareholding pattern

items.statement: Buyback will be considered under revised SEBI rules
items.quote: buyback, yes 29 definitely, we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market

items.statement: Clearing/settlement separation not required under PSS Act; only registration needed, no financial impact
items.quote: There is no question of any separation because this narrative is coming where SEBI requires the separation of the clearing and settlement function for the stock exchanges. But the Power Market Regulations just say one thing, that you have to comply with the PSS Act for the clearing function and the PSS Act is totally silent on whether there has to be a separate entity.

items.statement: I-REC growth driven by hourly stamping, RE100, GHG Scope 2, and upcoming SBTi recognition
items.quote: In the near future, we will have hourly-based time stamping available for I-RECs. Also, in India and in some of the international markets they have already started doing the pilots. Those are going to drive the demands throughRE100 claims, GHG Scope 2 claims and SBTi

items.statement: Targeting INR6,000-6,500 crores disbursement for FY27
items.quote: So, we are looking at anywhere between INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: Maintaining credit cost guidance of 2.5-3% for FY27; net credit cost expected closer to 2%
items.quote: Very much. We are at, as I said, 2.1% for Q1 and the efforts are on to retain that.

items.statement: Opex target ~INR675 crores for FY27 (down from INR760 crores FY26); ~10% increase in FY28
items.quote: So against the last year full opex of about INR760-odd crores. I think we should be more around INR675 crores or so for the full year this year. And next year should be just a 10% increase on that.

items.statement: INR545 crores sanctioned under CGS scheme; INR200 crores utilized; more sanctions in pipeline
items.quote: We managed to garner around INR545 crores of sanction under the credit guarantee scheme, and sanctions are still coming, and there are quite a few sanctions in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: NIM improved to 12.5% from 9.9% QoQ; yield at 24.6% (target 25.25%); marginal cost of borrowing down to 11.3% from 12%
items.quote: With the improving trend in the yield and declining borrowing cost, our NIM improved to 12.5% compared to 9.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: CGS borrowing priced at ~10% or slightly above; overall cost of borrowing down to 12.8% from 13.2%
items.quote: Pricing is just about at 10% or a little over 10% because there are sub-10%, there are marginally over 10% as well.

items.statement: Balance rights issue INR200 crores (INR100 cr promoter, INR100 cr others) expected this quarter
items.quote: The balance rights issue money of INR200 crores, INR100 crores from the promoter and the balance INR100 crores from others who participated is expected this quarter, before the end of this quarter.

items.statement: NBFC AUM long-term CAGR target of 20-25% after 1-2 year transition
items.quote: So, our aim is to increase at an CAGR of about 20-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target Rs 6,000-8,000 crores in 5 years at 20% CAGR
items.quote: So, if we grow 20%, we will have revenue in five years' time around Rs. 6,000 to Rs. 8,000 crores.

items.statement: NBFC secured book now 75% of AUM, up 5% YoY; yields rising with mix shift
items.quote: So, as you will see, even at the end of quarter-end the secured book constitutes 75% of the AUM, which is slightly higher than the last quarter-ended and even year-on-year, the secured book has grown by 5%.

items.statement: NBFC borrowing cost down 25 bps in Q1; NIM expected to grow gradually
items.quote: So, regarding the interest rate, so basically in the current quarter, we had a reduction in our weighted cost of fund by around 25 basis points.

items.statement: Insurance gross premium Rs 759 crores in Q1, 90% from non-life segment
items.quote: The major segment is our non-life insurance, which contributes approximately 90% of the total premium.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM grew 11.5% to Rs 4,787 crores; 92,129 active SIPs
items.quote: Our mutual fund AUM grew from 4,294 crores as on March '26 to Rs. 4,787 crores as on 30th June, representing a growth of approximately 11.5%.

items.statement: Insurance EBIT moderated due to manpower and distribution investments for reinsurance opportunity
items.quote: The moderated EBIT growth versus revenue reflects investments in distribution capacity and technology infrastructure to support the upcoming reinsurance opportunity following our composite broker upgrade.

items.statement: Stoxkart revenue quadrupled YoY to Rs 20 crores; added 26,000 subscription clients
items.quote: If you compare Q1 2025 to Q1 2026, it contributed around 20 crores. In Q1 2026, we contributed 20 crores in terms of revenue. And as number of clients, we opened around 26,000 clients in the quarter.

items.statement: Gift City business expanding; major player with good prospects
items.quote: Moreover, we are very optimistic about our Gift City businesses. This is expanding. So, in years to come, Gift City is having good prospects. And we are a major player in Gift City.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 26.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On a standalone basis, Q1 FY27 operational income stood at Rs. 273.4 crores, up 11.1% YoY, with an EBITDA of Rs. 71.5 crores, at a margin of 26.2%, an expansion of 100 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Expect employee cost growth of 22% to 24% for full year FY27 including ESOP expenses
items.quote: However, if you look at on a full year basis, including ESOP expenses, we expect that on a full year basis, employee cost growth can be in the range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Gross yield settled at around 88 basis points after regulatory changes from April 2026
items.quote: As a result, our gross yield has now settled at around 88 basis points.

items.statement: Current quarter margin is representative for next three quarters as regulatory adjustments are complete
items.quote: So regarding the margin, I tell you, you can probably consider the current quarter as a representative of margin.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book increased to INR1,240 crores in July from INR1,203 crores in June 2026
items.quote: Our monthly SIP book has further increased to around INR1,240 crores when I'm talking to you.

items.statement: Added around 600 distribution partners per month in Q1 FY27 versus 430 monthly run rate in FY26
items.quote: During the first quarter of current year, which is FY27, we added around 600 partners per month compared to monthly run rate of 430 in FY26.

items.statement: SIF AUM crossed INR500 crores with 1,323 distributors SIF certified as of June 2026
items.quote: Now today, if I talk about our SIF AUM has already crossed around INR500 crores. Now we already have around 1,400 around kind of SIF certified partners.

items.statement: PMS and AIF AUM stands at INR1,900 crores, up 37% year-on-year
items.quote: Coming to alternatives, I think number is roughly about INR1,900 crores, which we have as of now. So overall mutual -- the PMS and AIF AUM, what we are managing at the end of this quarter is INR1,900 crores.

items.statement: Plan to add around 30 new branches during FY27, over 12 already operationalized in Q1
items.quote: We plan to add around 30 new branches during the year, of which almost more than 12 branches have already been operationalized during the quarter.

items.statement: Regulatory changes creating opportunity as non-GST distributors face income reduction and seek platform support
items.quote: The recent regulatory changes are also creating incremental opportunity for us from a distributor growth perspective. Non-GST registered distributors who are working directly with the AMC have seen a meaningful reduction in their net income under the new structure.

items.statement: Direct-indirect AUM split is roughly 90-10 with 90% serviced by partners
items.quote: Direct AUM roughly about -- and the direct-indirect split would be roughly about you can say 90-10 kind of a thing. 90% of the AUM is serviced by partners and 10% includes the Indus, Karvy, Prudent's old B2C and iFAST.

items.statement: Commission and fee expenses grew 9.8% year-on-year due to regulatory changes including GST treatment and removal of 5 bps exit load
items.quote: Commission and fee expenses grew at a slower pace of 9.8%. This was primarily due to regulatory changes, which has been implemented from April 2026 related to GST treatment and removal of 5 basis points of exit load, which was part of TER earlier.

items.statement: Current AUM stands at roughly INR1.4 lakh crores, up nearly 16% from FY26 average of INR1.21 lakh crores
items.quote: While today, our AUM stands at roughly about INR1.4 lakh crores. So this represents a growth of nearly 16%.

items.statement: Expect current yield and margin to continue for foreseeable future with possible 1-2 bps decline over medium to long term
items.quote: Of course, over time, with the size of down the commercial will come down, but that is mainly on a new business. Obviously, over medium to long term, it may go down by 1, 2 basis points.

items.statement: Full year AUM growth guidance of 20% will be achieved comfortably
items.quote: And at this pace of quarterly growth, we should be able to achieve our full year growth guidance very comfortably.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 is 1.7% to 1.9%, trending towards 1.7%
items.quote: The guidance what we have given for the credit cost for this financial year, the credit cost will be in somewhere between 1.7% to 1.9%.

items.statement: Gross NPAs guided to fall below 3% in FY27
items.quote: We have also clearly guided you on the gross NPAs, which will fall to sub 3%.

items.statement: FY28 credit cost expected to be 1.6% to 1.7%
items.quote: From FY28 onwards, it won't be at 1.7%, 1.9% levels, which will -- even the highest range will be 1.7%, possibly around 1.6% to 1.7%.

items.statement: Opex to assets ratio to stay at 5.75%-6% in FY27, steady state 5.25%-5.5% from FY28
items.quote: I think we will stay at around 5.75% to 6% for this year. But in a steady state, this number should drop somewhere close to about 5.25% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Write-offs guided at INR 225-250 crores for FY27, running at INR 55-60 crores per quarter
items.quote: We should be seeing write-offs for the full year at somewhere around INR225 crores to INR 250 crores, which is largely the run rate that we did in the first quarter.

items.statement: Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at 1.75%-1.8% on book
items.quote: We will endeavor to maintain an overall coverage of 1.75% to 1.8% on the book.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing expected around 8.5%, with 10-15 bps further compression possible
items.quote: I think our incremental cost of borrowing should be somewhere around the 8.5% level, which means we still have another 20-30 basis points of compression that can come in the borrowings over the period.

items.statement: Yield on assets to settle around 22.25% after another 10-15 bps compression over next couple of quarters
items.quote: So maybe you will see this contraction of another 10-15 basis points for the next couple of quarters, should settle somewhere around the 22.25% levels.

items.statement: Spreads to remain flat at current levels for next few quarters assuming no policy rate changes
items.quote: Spread should largely remain flat to current levels for the next few quarters, assuming no policy actions.

items.statement: Branch additions of 50-60 branches planned for FY27, added 12 in Q1
items.quote: I don't think we are expecting to put too many branches this year. We'll continue our normal run rate of about 50-60 branches.

items.statement: No dearth of demand in the segment; demand was never a problem
items.quote: The first point to keep in mind is there is no dearth of demand in this segment which is something that we have been consistently reiterating. The demand was always there.

items.statement: Target ticket size mix of 25% at INR 3 lakh, 50% at INR 5 lakh, 25% at INR 10 lakh
items.quote: We definitely want to operate at 25-50-20, which will be 25% at around INR3 lakh ticket size and 50% around the INR5 lakh ticket size and the other 25% closer to the INR10 lakh ticket size.

items.statement: Planning to launch one new product in next 3-6 months, separate from existing housing product
items.quote: We are very clearly thinking 2-3 products, out of that one product which we wanted to go first, maybe in next 3 months or 6 months. We will definitely get into one of the products.

items.statement: Energy cost increases and regulatory liquidity decisions are key risks to monitor
items.quote: One is on the energy cost, which has gone up, which may even go up. Second is on the liquidity front, what the regulator is going to take a call on the price hike.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters (medium term)
items.quote: I would probably think it's in the medium term, maybe another 6 to 8 quarters from here onwards.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 18-20% CAGR maintained; EBITDA margin target of 40-45% with 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27
items.quote: We continue to maintain that we have a robust pipeline of sales where revenue will continue to be in the range of 18% to 20% CAGR. EBITDA margins will be in the range of 40% to 45%. We will maintain 40% threshold including Ascent by the end of this year.

items.statement: EBITDA growth visibility of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15% for FY27, better than previous forecast
items.quote: have visibility for EBITDA growth closer to 20 %, anywhere between 17% to 20%, and our PAT numbers anywhere between 12% to 15%. So, we are actually confident to deliver better results than what we had initially forecasted and guided

items.statement: Ascent EBITDA margin at ~8.4% in Q1 FY27; targeting double-digit margins within 12 months, EBITDA accretive by end of FY27 or early FY28
items.quote: In terms of the margin of the entity itself, it had already turned the corner into the previous quarter, as you heard from the Q4 of the previous year. This year, too, it continues to be around 8.4% in terms of the EBITDA margin, and we believe that in quarters to come, we would expand that.

items.statement: KFin consolidated EBITDA margin 34.2% including Ascent, 39.4% excluding Ascent in Q1 FY27; cost optimization benefits visible from Q2
items.quote: If you look at EBITDA margins, EBITDA has gone up overall at 7.1% year-on-year and 5.1% quarter-on-quarter. And this is something which we continue to work upon where the margins have come down because of Ascent integration. But without Ascent integration, they are good at 39.4%, while with Ascent, it is 34.2%.

items.statement: Won 6 new fund managers with $100M+ AUM each at Ascent in Q1 FY27; transitions from incumbents taking 3-5 months
items.quote: As I called out, what is probably the most heartwarming performance is the win of six mandates of fund managers who are above $100 million.

items.statement: Signed tech deals worth ~INR 40 crore total top-line in Q1 FY27 with delivery over 3-15 months; INR 25 crore big data deal over 18 months
items.quote: We have, in the previous quarter, have signed deals worth roughly about INR 40 crores in total top-line, which some will be done in 3 months, some 6 months, some 15 months, so on and so forth.

items.statement: International business (ex-Ascent) grew 32% YoY; Ascent revenue grew 200% YoY to $5.9M in Q1 FY27; targeting >25% growth
items.quote: In terms of international business, obviously with the Ascent's expansion, we have grown nearly 200% year-on-year. Even if you exclude Ascent, just the KFin's organic business has grown over 32%.

items.statement: Mutual fund industry AUM grew ~15% YoY in Q1; KFin grew ~16% YoY, gaining 80bps equity AUM market share
items.quote: For the Q1, the industry had grown a little around 15% on the overall AUM, even as KFin Tech has grown a little over 16%, so it is 100 basis points fast growth at the overall AUM level.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue share rose to 38% in Q1 FY27 from 24.5% in Q1 FY26; mutual fund fee revenue down to 55% from 66%
items.quote: If you look at contribution of non-MF revenue, it has gone up to 38%, which was 24.5% in Q1 of FY '26. There is growth across various segment of businesses.

items.statement: Yield declined ~2% QoQ in Q1 FY27; ~30% due to debt-to-liquid shift, ~70% due to contract renewal provisions; pricing discounts stable
items.quote: I think the debt-to-liquid is a substantive movement into the previous quarter. I think from a yield, the 2% impact that you have seen, about 30% of that impact is attributed to the movement from debt-to-liquid itself, okay, which then obviously means that it is about 1.7% is net of the asset class movement.

items.statement: Setting up Cayman Islands facility for regulatory substance requirements; near-term cost already baked in
items.quote: The organization has, you know, we are to start our facility in Cayman Islands in terms of a substance requirement that has come through as a part of the regulatory requirements, which means that we are going to have feet on street in Cayman Islands as well.

items.statement: Corporate actions tepid in Q2 FY27 due to top-tier IT firms not declaring dividends; retail investor participation still weak
items.quote: I would even guide to slightly tepid corporate action movement into at least the next quarter, as you may have seen that several top-tier IT services companies have decided not to declare dividends.

items.statement: Digital asset fund AUM markdowns due to crypto decline offset by new fund wins at Ascent; digital assets ~15% of AUM
items.quote: As I said, the digital currency funds have seen a certain amount of write-downs, markdowns, because of the crypto value coming down quite a bit, as you might have tracked to it.

items.statement: Pensions business broke even in Q4 FY26, now ~15%+ EBITDA margin; managing 2.5M+ pension accounts; won BPI contract in Philippines
items.quote: In the previous quarter, we have broken even. We continue to consolidate in terms of driving the margins in this line of business. It is no longer a loss-making, but adds to about roughly 15% plus in terms of the EBITDA.

items.statement: Wealth management platform mPower won 3 mandates in transition; dual revenue model: fixed-fee implementation + bps on AUM
items.quote: In the first commercial model, it will largely be a fixed-fee contract. It is almost like a platform implementation followed by the AMC, which can be 20%, 25%, 35% of the contract value, depending upon the complexity. In the second model, we charge basis points on the assets under management.

items.statement: Alternatives platform XAt manages 731 funds with 37.3% market share; pipeline may push to 40%; GIFT City forte
items.quote: Our total consolidated count of the funds today is roughly around 731, and it occupies a share of about 37.3%. The wins that we have, which are yet to launch, if we add that, we believe that the market share will be closing in on 40%.

items.statement: Cost of operations guidance of 25 bps reduction this year over 150 bps reduction since listing
items.quote: Cost of operations have been calibrated in a downward sloping curve and we continue our guidance of a 25-basis point reduction this year over the 150-basis point reduction we've delivered since listing.

items.statement: Spreads improved 39 bps to 9.4% driven by lower cost of borrowing and better asset pricing
items.quote: Capital allocation discipline helped us protect spreads, which improved by 39 bps at 9.4% driven by both a lower cost of borrowing and better pricing on the asset side.

items.statement: NIMs moved up by similar basis points as spreads to 10.6%
items.quote: NIMs moved up by a similar basis point as spreads and stood at 10.6% even as absolute borrowings increased, proof that growing the balance sheet and protecting the margin aren't mutually exclusive, just occasionally in tension.

items.statement: Branch expansion plan of 10-15 branches for the year after adding 5 in Q1
items.quote: So, this year should be between 10-15 branches, three, four up and down based on what the supervisors generally request you to and you approve. That's the plan.

items.statement: Login to disbursal conversion moderated to 34% from 42% due to inflation denting disposable income
items.quote: We've seen this show up in our login to disbursal conversion which moderated to 34% from 42%.

items.statement: Sub-10 lakh segment showing signs of leveraged stress warranting close monitoring
items.quote: The sub-10 lakh segment in particular is showing signs of leveraged stress and warrants close monitoring.

items.statement: Stage 2 ECL increased to 16% from 6%, total provisioning at 1.91% of assets, roughly 2x regulatory requirement
items.quote: As flagged in our last call, we took Stage 2 ECL up to 16% from 6%, bringing total provisioning to assets at 1.91% - The highest we've taken to date and roughly twice the regulatory requirement.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain range-bound at 1.4-1.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, so we are penciling in that it will be range-bound in this current range. So, 1.4% or 1.5%, this is the range that we are looking at for at least next two quarters.

items.statement: Opex guidance of 25 bps reduction for the year unchanged, targeting 4% or below by year-end
items.quote: The guidance for the year of 25 bps reduction remains unchanged.

items.statement: Co-origination mix reset to 10% following revised guidelines, expected to return to usual run rate from current quarter
items.quote: Following the revised guidelines, the co-origination mix reset to 10%. This has since stabilized and we expect a return to the usual run rate from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Cost of funds came down 90 bps year on year aided by repo rate cut transmission
items.quote: Aided by the transmission of repo rate cuts, our cost of funds has come down by about 90 basis points year on year.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 11% Q-o-Q to INR 2,631 crores, MSME AUM grew 4.5% Q-o-Q to INR 9,271 crores
items.quote: loan against gold AUM is at INR 2,631 crores with a growth of 11% on Q-o-Q basis. We added five branches during the quarter, bringing the total branch count to 256 as on June 2026

items.statement: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps during quarter, expected to stabilize this quarter before pullback in subsequent quarters
items.quote: On asset quality, 0+ rose by 70 bps during the quarter and that's our homework for the current quarter. The momentum on rollbacks is better and we should stabilize here for a quarter before a pullback in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Guidance for coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts
items.quote: We close the quarter at 14.7% ROE and our guidance for the coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts.

items.statement: Yield range expected to stabilize at 17.50% to 17.75%
items.quote: That's our range where the yields generally stabilize. One good quarter of either product gives a 10-15 bps up and down. So, that's the range we will be at and which ensures that at say current cost of fund 10 bps up and down will give you a spread of more than 9

items.statement: No plans to add new products, will focus on improving existing small ticket LAP and gold loan business
items.quote: No, we keep doing what we are doing. We have to get better at what we are doing. We still have a lot of work to do in that. So, we will keep focusing. We have learned something over the last 8 years, and once you've learned it, hopefully over the next 8 years you will better it. So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new. We will continue doing what we are doing. Hopeful

items.statement: Top line expected to grow in line with stated guidance of mid-teens; FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid -teens. We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organizational capabilities while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26.

items.statement: Management reviewing mid-teens guidance upward to high teens and EBITDA margin of 18% over 2 years
items.quote: I would rather want to step it up from mid -teens, it may go even higher to high teens and an EBITDA margin of 18%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%; like-to-like gross margin 48.4% (up 522 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 277 basis points to 46%, supported by a favorable input cost environment and early benefits from backward integration despite the temporary impact of global supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: India-UK FTA expected to improve margins by 70-80 bps in FY27 and 130-140 bps in FY28
items.quote: We expect the benefit to flow in second half of the year and would lead to about 70 to 80 basis points improvement in current financial year. For FY28 on a full year basis, it would help us in improving margins by 130 to 140 basis points.

items.statement: Premiumization remains a structural trend; ABD outperformed industry in P&A (10.7% vs low single digits) and Mass Premium (2.3% vs stable)
items.quote: Importantly, ABD's volume performance was ahead of the industry where the P&A segment grew in the low single digits and Mass Premium and others remained broadly stable on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value in Q1 FY27 vs 46.2% and 55.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, the Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value compared to 46.2% and 55.8% respectively in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: ICONiQ White grew 33.8% to 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27; targeting ~15 million cases in FY27
items.quote: ICONiQ White continues to lead this momentum. The brand delivered 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27 compared to 2.3 million cases in Q1 FY26 with a monthly average of 1 million plus cases resulting in a growth of 33.8% in the quarter on year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Launching deluxe vodka and premium whisky in H2 FY27 to fill white spaces
items.quote: There is a vodka market of 15 million to 18 million case s, where there is a brand leader which is unchallenged. It is a high contribution segment and now ABD can make foray into this space, this in H2 FY27. We will also come up with a premium Whisky in H2 FY 27 which will again be a uniquely packaged product with a new concept altogether.

items.statement: International footprint expanded to 39 countries in Q1 FY27 from 36 in Q4 FY26; exports asset-light with superior working capital efficiency
items.quote: ABD has expanded its footprint to 39 countries in Q1 FY 27 compared to 36 countries in Q4 FY 26, reinforcing our position as one of India's leading spirits exporters by volume.

items.statement: Telangana overdues ~₹400 crores; recent supplies paid on time, older overdues largely cleared, dialogue ongoing for price increase
items.quote: Overdue from Telangana government is approximate ₹400 crores. So right now, what's happening is Telangana is paying us well within agreed timeline for all recent supplies. Whereas for the overdue before 2024 has been paid up.

items.statement: Price increase dialogue ongoing with Telangana and 1-2 other states; guardrails built in case price hikes don't materialize

items.quote: Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

items.statement: ABD Maestro FY26 revenue ~₹40 crores, expected to double in FY27; minimum 3-year gestation for luxury portfolio
items.quote: we clocked in FY 26 was top line of ~₹40 crores, which we expect to double in FY27. So that is an indication of how the business is moving forward. items.statement: Reiterated FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.

items.quote: it's basically the mix which is driving this. You know, the as you see there's a significant improvement in margins which primarily coming from higher contribution from the drug device combination business

items.statement: Demand for semaglutide generics significantly outpaces supply in Canada and India; customer forecasts remain robust
items.quote: The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand. In fact, the demand has been significantly outpacing supply both in the markets where the brand was present or was launching.

items.quote: the lines are driven by the CSA. That's we have always said that the mix of the company is going to be driven by significantly more CSA.

items.quote: this first half itself, we will be taking a shutdown on our one of our sterile injectable sites basically to add this capacity. So, you will see, this addition will be a significant contributor to our FY28 numbers.

items.statement: EBITDA trajectory to continue upward beyond FY28 driven by biologics commercialization from FY29, Europe/US market entry, and capacity expansions
items.quote: One clear answer for you is that yes, our EBITDA trajectory will continue to go upward beyond FY28. And this is going to be dependent on all our modalities, which all our service offerings.

items.quote: our RFP funnel today is almost 4x of what it was just over a year ago. And this spans across innovators, biosimilars, as well as animal health companies.

items.quote: we are also going to be taking some other capacity expansion because we see our current biologics capacity will require expansion. So, we are going to be expanding both the mammalian as well as microbial capacity.

items.quote: the lines what we have added, even when we had started this program of adding capacity, the idea was line, all lines should be able to cater to all our customers.

items.quote: you will see this as a sequential quarter-on-quarter improvement in our revenue and in EBITDA.

items.quote: thanks to all these, we are able to actually pull demand into this quarter, therefore, which is what the timeline which Dr. Reddy's has shared publicly. And therefore, thanks to that we have had, we don't anticipate any impact on our supplies.

items.statement: 12 successful regulatory inspections and customer audits in Q1 including two surprise FDA audits across two sites
items.quote: We had 12 successful inspections this quarter across regulatory inspections and customer audits, including two surprise FDA audits across two of our sites.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 140-160 crores for FY27
items.quote: On the capital expenditure side, we are on plan to use our IPO proceeds as per the stated objects therein, and we will probably maintain the range we have said earlier, about INR 140 crores to INR 160 crores per year of capital expenditure, even in this financial year.

items.statement: Won two multi-year PSU bank tenders worth INR 73 crores
items.quote: In this quarter, we won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 due to higher material costs
items.quote: Gross profit increased by 13.3% to INR 157 crores. Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 135 bps YoY to 25.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y. Despite the pressure on gross margin, disciplined management of employee and other operating costs supported profitability.

items.statement: 40-45% of gross margin impact from currency, rest from war-driven commodity and logistics costs

items.statement: Actively working with customers on price revisions to protect margins
items.quote: As of now, we operate in a challenging environment impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures. While these factors may create some near-term headwinds, we are actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger due to seasonal BFSI pickup and steady communication and IoT momentum
items.quote: Looking ahead, given the nature of our business, we expect H2 FY27 to be stronger driven by seasonal pickup in BFSI demand, and steady momentum in the communication and fulfillment businesses, and continued growth in the IoT segment.

items.statement: Bengaluru metal card facility expected operational by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: We would like to update that our Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities are still under construction. We expect the Bengaluru facility to be operational by the end of the calendar year after the necessary regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization 65-70% on average, peaking at 85-90% during high demand periods
items.quote: Capacity utilization, typically for us, in our business currently is around 65% to 70%. Having said that, this also has a cyclical nature to it. So, typically, when customers have higher renewal cycle demands or there are month-end loads of customers, we also reach about 85% to 90% of our capacity utilization, but on average we tend to be in the 65% to 70% range.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 357.63 crore as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility beyond 24 months due to 3-5 year contract life cycles.
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order books stood at Rs. 357.63 crores. Since our contracts are 3-5 years in life cycle, these order books provide visibility beyond 24 months.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin improved to 10.5% from 7% in FY25; Q4 FY26 PAT margin improved to 15.1% from 8.7% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Profit after tax for the year stood at Rs. 24 crores, representing a robust 70% year-on-year growth, while PAT margin improved to 10.5% compared with 7% in previous financial year.

items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.5 per equity share for Financial Year 26, subject to shareholders' approval at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Strategy prioritizes continued investment in technology infrastructure, proprietary platforms, AI/ML capabilities, and skilled workforce for complex digital transformation programs.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our strategy remains focused on four key priorities: 1. Continue investing in strengthening our technology infrastructure and proprietary products and platforms. 2.
